item.title: Mercado financiero argentino repunta en ámbito contagiado por 'efecto Brasil'
item.description: Los activos de Argentina recuperaban ligeramente terreno el martes tras el fuerte derrumbe de la víspera cuando los precios reflejaron la sorpresa por el resultado electoral en el vecino Brasil, principal socio comercial del país austral.
item.dc:creator: Jorge Otaola
item.content:encoded: Los activos de Argentina recuperaban ligeramente terreno el martes tras el fuerte derrumbe de la víspera cuando los precios reflejaron la sorpresa por el resultado electoral en el vecino Brasil, principal socio comercial del país austral. La victoria en las urnas del reelecto presidente socialista Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva no estaba previsto por las encuestadoras, las que daban triunfador al liberal Flávio Bolsonaro, senador de derecha alineado al mandatario argentino Javier Milei. Esta situación disparó el riesgo país de Argentina al máximo en un año y disparó órdenes de ventas sobre acciones y bonos soberanos dado que el panorama financiero y económico en la región pasa a otro plano, ante el público cortocircuito político entre Milei y Lula. El real brasileño se devaluó fuerte el lunes y esto presiona sobre la competitividad de Argentina. "A las dudas económicas que ya pesan sobre la economía de Argentina, ahora se suma otro en las relaciones francas entre dos países que se necesitan mutuamente, quedando los argentinos en desventaja por el peso específico de cada país", respondió un analista financiero de un banco español con sede en Buenos Aires. "Pero más allá del efecto contagio de Brasil, el riesgo país que refleja Argentina es también por las dudas que pesan sobre el futuro de su economía, más los complejos vencimientos de deuda que se vienen y que presionan sobre las paridades de los bonos (domésticos)", acotó. Argentina elegirá presidente en 2027 con Milei lanzado en búsqueda de sus reelección, aunque hay miedos subyacentes por una eventual recesión técnica de la economía con el tercer trimestre del 2026, más la inaccesibilidad a los mercados internacionales desde hace años. El índice accionario MSCI Merval (.MMXMRVLGA) de la bolsa porteña pasaba a ganar un 0,7%, contra una caída del 2,9% en la víspera, y los bonos públicos extrabursátiles promediaban un ligero avance del 0,2%, luego de ceder el 0,6% el lunes. A su vez, el riesgo país reportado a diario por el banco J.P.Morgan se movía en los 758 puntos básicos (1425 GMT), luego de trepar a las 765 unidades en la ronda anterior y evidenciar niveles similares a los de un año atrás. El peso mayorista se apreciaba el 0,1% a 1.539,5 por dólar , aunque en su apertura anotó el piso récord de 1.550 unidades, ante un banco central (BCRA) que el lunes cortó una racha de 19 días consecutivos con compras de divisas para reforzar sus reservas internacionales. "El aumento del riesgo país impactando mayormente en los bonos largos de las curvas en dólares, tanto bajo ley local como ley externa. El deterioro se dio en línea con los débiles datos de actividad económica publicados la semana pasada y la sostenida incertidumbre acerca de la popularidad del Gobierno de cara a las elecciones de 2027", dijo Balanz. "La inesperada victoria del presidente de Brasil, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, en la segunda vuelta presidencial, le está poniendo presión adicional" al mercado argentino, señaló. Analistas locales coinciden en que la suerte de Lula, en su cuarto mandato presidencial, tendrá un impacto directo sobre la macroeconomía argentina, dado que el vecino país se dirige a una menor actividad en general, un elevado déficit fiscal y un Congreso en manos de la oposición. El Tesoro argentino buscará el miércoles renovar vencimiento de deuda a corto plazo por unos 10,8 billones de pesos (unos 7.000 millones de dólares), donde no se descarta un aumento en la tasa de interés dado los desfavorables vientos externos. A su vez, al cierre de los mercados también del miércoles, la gigante petrolera estatal YPF (YPFDm.BA) reportará sus números trimestrales a septiembre, donde se prevé que anuncie un aumento del 21,9% en sus ingresos a 5.658 millones de dólares, según la estimación media de analistas basada en datos de LSEG.

item.title: US Justice Dept asks Washington state not to count ballots from possible noncitizens
item.description: The US Justice Department has asked Washington state not to count any mail ballots received from more than 400 residents who it says may not be US citizens, opening a new front in the Trump administration's push to expand control of election administration ahead of the November 3 midterms.
item.dc:creator: Luc Cohen
item.content:encoded: The US Justice Department has asked Washington state not to count any mail ballots received from more than 400 residents who it says may not be US citizens, opening a new front in the Trump administration's push to expand control of election administration ahead of the November 3 midterms . The letter, which resembled a request earlier this month that [USN:L2N46C163 TEXT:"California"] not count any ballots received from around 20,000 alleged noncitizens, marked an escalation in the Trump administration's pressure on state election officials over alleged noncitizen voting. Multiple state audits and independent studies have found that voter fraud, including voting by noncitizens, is very rare and has not affected election outcomes. The pressure campaign is a rare intervention by the Justice Department in the voting process in the weeks before an election. President Donald Trump 's fellow Republicans are locked in a tight battle to retain slim majorities in both chambers of the US Congress, and centrist Democrat Marie Gluesenkamp Perez's campaign to hold onto her southwest Washington seat is one of [USN:L6N4670ZS TEXT:"10 key races"] that could decide control of the US House of Representatives. In the letter dated October 26, the top federal prosecutors in Seattle and Spokane asked Washington Secretary of State Steve Hobbs, the state's top elections official, to determine whether the more than 400 people were in fact US citizens and to not count their ballots until their citizenship was determined. The letter said the Justice Department would seek "emergency relief" if the state could not take those actions by noon local time (1900 GMT) on Wednesday. There were 5 million registered voters in Washington state as of 2024, according to the secretary of state's office. Hobbs' office did not immediately respond to a request for comment. In California, after state election officials said complying with the Justice Department's demand would be impractical and questioned the accuracy of its information on alleged noncitizens, federal prosecutors filed a lawsuit seeking to block the state from counting any ballots received from the alleged noncitizens. A hearing is scheduled in that case for 1 p.m. PDT (2000 GMT) on Tuesday before US District Judge David Carter in Los Angeles. A federal appeals court on Monday night denied the Justice Department's request to block California from counting any ballots before Carter had the chance to rule. Democrats and voting rights advocates say federal data on citizenship is often outdated, meaning naturalized citizens registered to vote are often mistakenly flagged as noncitizens. In its letter to Washington state officials, the Justice Department acknowledged that some of the individuals flagged as possible noncitizens may have since naturalized, but it did not say how many.

item.title: Una investigación de la ONU dice que Israel siguió cometiendo genocidio en Gaza tras la tregua
item.description: Israel siguió cometiendo genocidio en Gaza tras el alto el fuego negociado por Estados Unidos el pasado mes de octubre en el enclave, afirmó una comisión de la ONU en un informe publicado el lunes que Israel desestimó calificándolo de "campaña de desinformación".
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Israel siguió cometiendo genocidio en Gaza tras el alto el fuego negociado por Estados Unidos el pasado mes de octubre en el enclave, afirmó una comisión de la ONU en un informe publicado el lunes que Israel desestimó calificándolo de "campaña de desinformación". El informe de la Comisión Internacional Independiente de Investigación de la ONU sobre el Territorio Palestino Ocupado, incluida Jerusalén Oriental, e Israel, examinó las violaciones cometidas contra la población civil palestina, incluidos los niños, desde el inicio de la guerra entre Israel y Hamás el 7 de octubre de 2023 hasta septiembre. En él se afirma que las autoridades israelíes han seguido cometiendo "actos genocidas con la intención genocida de destruir, total o parcialmente, a la población palestina de Gaza", y que la situación también ha seguido deteriorándose en la Cisjordania ocupada. Otro informe de la comisión, publicado en septiembre del año pasado, concluyó que Israel había cometido genocidio en Gaza y que altos cargos israelíes, entre ellos el primer ministro Benjamin Netanyahu, habían incitado a cometer estos actos, acusaciones que Israel calificó de escandalosas. La misión israelí en Ginebra dijo que el último informe forma parte de una campaña de desinformación destinada a demonizar al Estado de Israel. "El intento de destruir el Estado judío (…) continúa hoy en día a través de los esfuerzos de actores como la Comisión de Investigación de la ONU para socavar la legitimidad de Israel y negarle su derecho fundamental a existir y a defenderse", declaró el embajador Daniel Meron en un comunicado. La comisión constató que las fuerzas israelíes continuaron utilizando munición pesada, drones, cuadricópteros, artillería y fuego de francotiradores en zonas densamente pobladas durante el alto el fuego en Gaza. Señaló que la "Línea Amarilla", que se presentó como una demarcación temporal del alto el fuego, se está adentrando cada vez más en Gaza y se está convirtiendo en una frontera de facto, lo que, según el informe, refleja la expansión del control territorial de Israel sobre Gaza.

item.title: Goldman vê manutenção de preços do diesel pela Petrobras após governo manter subsídios
item.description: O Goldman Sachs prevê que a Petrobras deverá manter os preços do diesel vendido a distribuidoras inalterados até o fim do ano, após o governo brasileiro ter decidido prorrogar por mais 30 dias os subsídios ao combustível.
item.dc:creator: Marta Nogueira
item.content:encoded: O Goldman Sachs prevê que a Petrobras (PETR3.SA) deverá manter os preços do diesel vendido a distribuidoras inalterados até o fim do ano, após o governo brasileiro ter decidido prorrogar por mais 30 dias os subsídios ao combustível. Em relatório a clientes nesta terça-feira, o banco afirmou que [USN:S0N44L00T TEXT:"a renovação do incentivo"] de R$2,12 por litro para produtores e importadores de diesel, somada a um subsídio adicional de R$1,40 por litro ainda disponível para importações até 6 de novembro, reduz a necessidade de a estatal elevar preços para acompanhar a alta das cotações internacionais. Os analistas estimam que o preço realizado do diesel pela Petrobras está atualmente em R$5,43 por litro, cerca de 25% abaixo da paridade internacional de importação, calculada em aproximadamente R$7,30 por litro. Ainda assim, eles destacaram que os incentivos maiores para o diesel importado permitem que distribuidoras consigam o combustível no exterior a preços próximos aos praticados pela Petrobras. "Essa assimetria pode reduzir, embora não eliminar, o escopo para um aumento de preços pela Petrobras", disseram analistas do Goldman Sachs em relatório. O Goldman Sachs reiterou ainda sua recomendação de compra para as ações da Petrobras.

item.title: Palestinos protestam contra demolições na Cisjordânia enquanto israelenses votam
item.description: Tropas israelenses lançaram nesta terça-feira uma granada de atordoamento para dispersar palestinos que se reuniram para protestar contra uma operação militar que desalojou milhares de moradores de um bairro em Hebron, na Cisjordânia ocupada por Israel.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Tropas israelenses lançaram nesta terça-feira uma granada de atordoamento para dispersar palestinos que se reuniram para protestar contra uma operação militar que desalojou milhares de moradores de um bairro em Hebron, na Cisjordânia ocupada por Israel. Os distúrbios se seguiram à morte de dois soldados israelenses baleados por atiradores palestinos em um posto de controle na semana passada. Eles também ocorreram enquanto os israelenses votavam em uma eleição na qual a postura do país na Cisjordânia tem sido uma importante questão política. Algumas autoridades palestinas acusaram o primeiro-ministro israelense Benjamin Netanyahu de lançar uma repressão na Cisjordânia para coincidir com a votação, como forma de mobilizar seus apoiadores de direita. O governo afirma que sua operação é uma resposta ao ataque contra seus soldados. Um grupo de homens, mulheres e crianças palestinos se reuniu no protesto de terça-feira. Um senhor idoso segurava um cartaz que dizia: “Não à punição coletiva, não aos bloqueios e não ao deslocamento”. As forças armadas afirmaram ter lançado uma granada de atordoamento para dispersá-los, de modo que a operação pudesse continuar. Na segunda-feira, as Nações Unidas informaram que mais de 3.000 palestinos foram forçados a deixar suas casas devido à operação militar israelense, que teve como alvo bairros próximos ao posto de controle onde homens armados palestinos mataram os dois soldados israelenses na sexta-feira. “A punição coletiva é uma grave violação do direito internacional”, afirmou o chefe de direitos humanos da ONU, Volker Türk, em comunicado. “Ameaças de esvaziar e apagar bairros inteiros também suscitam sérias preocupações quanto à limpeza étnica.” As forças armadas israelenses afirmaram em um comunicado no domingo que as tropas realizariam demolições na área. O comunicado informou que os soldados não localizaram nenhuma arma nas buscas realizadas nas casas. Desde o ataque de sexta-feira ao posto de controle, Israel bloqueou as entradas da maioria das cidades e vilas palestinas em toda a Cisjordânia, restringindo severamente a liberdade de movimento dos palestinos. Noura Nassar, uma moradora deslocada que participou dos protestos, disse que teve dificuldades para obter atendimento médico por causa dos bloqueios. “Onde está a democracia nisso tudo? As eleições deles são hoje, claro, mas e nós? Não somos seres humanos? Queremos sair, queremos ir ao médico”, disse Nassar. Netanyahu e seu principal rival, Gadi Eisenkot, se opõem à criação de um Estado palestino independente ao lado de Israel. Moradores expulsos do bairro de Hebron afirmaram que a eleição desta terça-feira em Israel pouco faria para mudar a realidade nos territórios que Israel ocupa desde 1967. “Entre eles, vão eleger quem é o opressor e quem vai destruir o povo palestino. Essa é a eleição deles”, disse Sana’ Salman Abu Sneineh, outro morador expulso. O governo de Netanyahu tem presidido a uma rápida expansão dos assentamentos israelenses, considerados ilegais por órgãos da ONU e pela maioria dos países, embora Israel conteste isso. Sob a coalizão de direita de Netanyahu, também houve um aumento da violência de colonos militantes contra os palestinos.

item.title: Fenerbahce condemn brawl after loss to Galatasaray
item.description: Fenerbahce condemned a brawl that broke out on the pitch after their 2-1 derby defeat by Galatasaray in the Turkish Super Lig on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Fenerbahce condemned a brawl that broke out on the pitch after their 2-1 derby defeat by Galatasaray in the Turkish Super Lig on Monday. Players and staff from both teams rushed onto the field after a scuffle between Fenerbahce's Kerem Akturkoglu and Galatasaray's Roland Sallai, according to video shared on social media. "The rivalry and tension of the derby do not give anyone the right to attack our players," Fenerbahce said in a statement. "What happened cannot be dismissed as 'derby tension.' The behaviour of the opposing team's members, instead of reducing tension, fuelled the incidents." Fenerbahce have called for an investigation and disciplinary action against those responsible for the brawl.

item.title: Critics attack 'anti-democratic' French bill making rioters pay
item.description: A proposed French law making rioters liable to pay up to €10,000 ($11,150) for damage they cause faces a backlash from rights groups and some lawyers who say it attacks the basic democratic right to take to the streets to protest.
item.dc:creator: Mark John, Layli Foroudi
item.content:encoded: A proposed French law making rioters liable to pay up to €10,000 ($11,150) for damage they cause faces a backlash from rights groups and some lawyers who say it attacks the basic democratic right to take to the streets to protest. President Emmanuel Macron's government, under pressure to quell social protests accompanied by some of France's worst unrest in years, says the law is needed to compensate victims of the vandalism that often follows protests, such as the looting and [USN:L1N46302B TEXT:"rioting"] seen across the country on October 17. But critics say the draft bill, being debated in parliament this week, is worded in such a way that legitimate protesters who happened to be close to the scene of any violence could also be deemed legally responsible for it and face prosecution. "Around the edges of a protest there can be those who engage in violence or damage with no involvement from the vast majority of peaceful, legitimate demonstrators," said Hanna Bouchareb, a Paris-based lawyer who represented some of those accused in fast-track trials of taking part in rioting on October 17. "It's very problematic because it undermines the right to protest," she told Reuters. The text states that anyone who knowingly formed part of a group of people would be held jointly responsible for any damage caused by any member of that group. It further allows the state to seize welfare entitlements of those convicted, or those of their parents if they are minors, to help pay the costs. French businesses and retailers say they have lost millions of euros either through looting or vandalism or by being forced to shut their shops and board their windows during protests. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez, who offered his resignation to Macron last week after security forces were overwhelmed by the unrest, rejected arguments the law undermined the principle that individuals were only accountable for their own actions. "What this draft law changes is that we are creating a joint responsibility - not a collective one," Nunez, whom Macron asked to remain at his post, told broadcaster TF1. That is a distinction rejected by France's Human Rights League (LDH) and a group of trade unionists who signed a column in Le Monde newspaper this weekend demanding it be scrapped. Police were accused in 2020 of using excessive force against "yellow vest" anti-government protesters and there was criticism then of a subsequently watered-down law banning circulation of images of police officers in some circumstances. In recent weeks, protesters have again accused police of heavy-handed tactics against the student protesters while lawyers including Bouchareb have raised legal concerns over the fast-tracked convictions of some of those accused of rioting. Backers of the proposed new law point to surveys showing broad public support for it. The National Rally (RN) party of Marine Le Pen - the far-right frontrunner for next year's presidential election - said it would go even further. "The vandal's law is good in that it recognises the principle of joint responsibility," RN senator Edwige Diaz told French television. "But not with a cap at 10,000 euros."

item.title: Sri Lanka beat Pakistan to reach final, England eliminated
item.description: Sri Lanka reached the final of the one-day international Tri-series in Pakistan with a comfortable eight-wicket victory over the hosts in Lahore on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Sri Lanka reached the final of the one-day international Tri-series in Pakistan with a comfortable eight-wicket victory over the hosts in Lahore on Tuesday. The result ensured England, who lost their first three matches, were knocked out of the tournament with a game to spare. Pakistan were dismissed for 110, Sri Lanka's left-arm seamer Dilshan Madushanka starred with the ball, claiming a career-best 5-34 to earn the player-of-the-match award. "We had a plan and followed it. Because of that, as a team, we were able to bowl them out for a low score," Madushanka said. England had shown signs of progress in the format this year, winning a series in Sri Lanka before home victories over India in July and Sri Lanka. Their campaign in Pakistan, however, unravelled in dramatic fashion. England failed to defend [USN:L1N4680Y6 TEXT:"429 against Sri Lanka"] despite captain Harry Brook scoring the fastest double century in ODI history and suffered another painful loss when Pakistan snatched a [USN:L6N46B07F TEXT:"one-wicket victory"] after Shadab Khan and Haris Rauf shared a record 89-run last-wicket partnership. England's final match of the series against Sri Lanka on Thursday will now be a dead rubber.

item.title: Brazil's markets recover some ground after selloff; minister vows fiscal discipline
item.description: Brazilian markets recovered some ground on Tuesday after a sharp selloff triggered by President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's reelection, while his government downplayed the previous day's turmoil as a temporary repositioning by investors and pledged to maintain fiscal responsibility.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Brazilian markets recovered some ground on Tuesday after a [USN:L2N46C051 TEXT:"sharp selloff"] triggered by President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's [USN:L2N46B01X TEXT:"reelection"], while his government downplayed the previous day's turmoil as a temporary repositioning by investors and pledged to maintain fiscal responsibility. The real strengthened nearly 2% against the US dollar to around 5.31 per greenback, after tumbling more than 11% in the previous session. The Bovespa (.BVSP) benchmark stock index rose 1% after ending Monday down 13.9%, while interest rate futures retreated. Finance Minister Dario Durigan said the recent market rout reflected positioning rather than a deterioration in Brazil's economic fundamentals, noting that investors had built up bets on a victory by right-wing presidential challenger Flavio Bolsonaro before Sunday's runoff. "Yesterday's reaction was much more about the positions the market had adopted in recent days," Durigan told reporters in Brasilia. "It was not a reaction to fundamentals." He said calmer trading on Tuesday suggested markets were becoming more rational, adding that he had been in contact with financial market participants. Durigan also sought to reassure investors that the government remained committed to fiscal responsibility. Markets plunged on Monday after Lula secured a fourth non-consecutive term, wiping out gains accumulated during a rally fueled by expectations of a victory by Bolsonaro, who was ahead of the incumbent president after the first round of voting on October 4. Investors have since focused on whether the incoming administration can deliver credible fiscal adjustment while preserving social spending and investment, as well as on Lula's selection of key economic officials. JPMorgan analysts said markets had yet to develop a clear narrative for Lula's fourth administration beyond the sharp correction in asset prices, but argued investors would likely reassess the outlook in coming weeks as the new government's economic team and policy plans take shape. "And we dare to say that as much as the market is adverse now, it will construct a story that leads equity markets forward," they wrote in a note to clients. Alfredo Menezes, a partner at asset manager Armor Capital, said the selloff had created attractive entry points for investors. "When stop-loss moves happen in the market, dozens of opportunities emerge. Emotion does not talk to reason," Menezes wrote on X, adding that shares of some companies he considers high-quality assets had fallen as much as 36%.

item.title: Nigeria panel says 37 detained miners died from overcrowding and neglect
item.description: A group of 37 suspected illegal miners died in detention in Nigeria as a result of severe overcrowding, poor ventilation and neglect, according to a government investigation into their deaths.
item.dc:creator: Camillus Eboh
item.content:encoded: A group of 37 suspected illegal miners died in detention in Nigeria as a result of severe overcrowding, poor ventilation and neglect, according to a government investigation into their deaths. The investigating committee, set up after the deaths last month sparked outrage in Nigeria, rejected earlier claims by officials that an outbreak of disease was to blame and called for compensation for victims and survivors as well as an overhaul of the agency involved. The deaths, which included many teenagers working in artisanal gold mines, [USN:L6N45A0EV TEXT:"triggered protests"] in Nigeria, raising fresh concerns about [USN:S8N38T08D TEXT:"conditions in detention facilities"] and the treatment of suspects awaiting trial. Jonathan Kure, chairman of the committee, said the deaths were "entirely preventable" and a result of severe overcrowding, deprivation of basic necessities and ignored warnings. "The tragedy demonstrates the consequences of systemic disregard for detention standards, supervisory responsibilities, and the welfare of persons in custody," Kure said after his committee reviewed evidence, including detention records, autopsies, hospital reports and communication logs. NSCDC officials did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The evidence showed the victims died from asphyxia, an acute respiratory failure caused by prolonged confinement in a severely overcrowded, poorly ventilated cell, worsened by heat stress and dehydration, Kure said. "The evidence did not support claims that the deaths resulted from a disease outbreak," Kure said. The Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), the paramilitary agency that locked up the miners as part of efforts to regulate mining, initially suggested the detainees may have died from an unspecified disease before later saying the cause had not been established. The panel recommended 30 million naira (about $22,500) in compensation for each victim's family and 10 million naira for each of the 41 survivors. The findings are in line [USN:L1N45E0IV TEXT:"with testimonies"] from survivors who told Reuters that dozens of artisanal miners were crammed into a small holding cell and repeatedly ignored after complaining of overcrowding. The government has suspended senior NSCDC officials pending the investigation, but the panel called for a sweeping overhaul of the agency's leadership. ($1 = 1,337.5900 naira)

item.title: Autoridades Venezuela esperan que crecimiento PIB se ubique entre 6% y 10% en 2027
item.description: El Gobierno y el Banco Central de Venezuela dijeron el martes que esperan que la economía crezca entre un 6% y un 10% en 2027, manteniendo el impulso que ha mostrado en los últimos años tras un largo periodo de contracción.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El Gobierno y el Banco Central de Venezuela dijeron el martes que esperan que la economía crezca entre un 6% y un 10% en 2027, manteniendo el impulso que ha mostrado en los últimos años tras un largo periodo de contracción. La economía venezolana ha repuntado este año en parte por el impulso que ha tenido el sector petrolero tras los acuerdos con Estados Unidos y empresas energéticas de otros países, pero aún la recuperación dista de la registrada hace más de una década, según analistas. El Ministerio de Finanzas y el Banco Central dijeron en un comunicado que buscan que la inflación se ubique en un rango de dos dígitos para el cierre del próximo año, sin dar detalles. Venezuela registra actualmente una inflación de 465%, de acuerdo con los datos oficiales, debido a la acelerada depreciación del tipo de cambio, lo que golpea los ingresos de las familias. El país petrolero, que no publicaba proyecciones económicas desde hace unos 10 años, ha reanudado sus relaciones con el Fondo Monetario Internacional (FMI) y ha estado actualizando parte de los datos económicos. El acuerdo de políticas señala que en 2027 se incrementará "el peso de fuentes de financiamiento externas y movilización de recursos internos compatibles con los objetivos fiscales y de inflación". La presidenta encargada de Venezuela, Delcy Rodríguez, quien asumió el poder luego que Nicolás Maduro fuera capturado en enero por fuerzas estadounidenses, espera que el país reciba unos 12.000 millones de dólares en financiamientos en los próximos años. El país ha estado[USN:L6N4661C8 TEXT:" explorando opciones "]para pagar a sus acreedores y entre ellas se encuentra gestionar un préstamo puente con Qatar para cancelar al Banco Interamericano de Desarrollo y así obtener nuevos financiamientos. Venezuela anunció en mayo una reestructuración de la deuda que podría superar los 200.000 millones de dólares. Las obligaciones incluyen bonos, préstamos de instituciones multilaterales, laudos arbitrales, préstamos bilaterales y deuda comercial.

item.title: Syngenta IPO aims for valuation of at least $66 billion, sources say
item.description: Syngenta's advisers are targeting a valuation of at least $66 billion in the Swiss-Chinese agrochemicals group's planned Hong Kong listing, which is likely to take place early next year, two people familiar with the matter told Reuters.
item.dc:creator: John Revill, Oliver Hirt
item.content:encoded: Syngenta's advisers are targeting a valuation of at least $66 billion in the Swiss-Chinese agrochemicals group's planned Hong Kong listing, which is likely to take place early next year, two people familiar with the matter told Reuters. UBS (UBSG.S) and China International Capital Corp (CICC) are marketing the Basel-based maker of seeds and crop-protection products at 15 to 20 times expected 2026 core earnings (EBITDA), the sources said. That would value Syngenta, which is controlled by Chinese state-owned firm Sinochem (600500.SS) , at $66 billion to $88 billion, based on its 2025 EBITDA of $4.4 billion, placing the offering among the largest global IPOs expected next year. The valuation reflects Syngenta's efforts to position itself more as a biotechnology company than a chemicals producer, the sources said. One of them added that a strong product line-up in crop protection and development pipeline for new seed varieties resistant to disease and pests supported a high valuation. China CITIC Bank and Bank of America are also helping run the IPO. Syngenta and UBS declined to comment. CICC, China CITIC Bank and Bank of America did not immediately respond to requests. JANUARY WINDOW Three sources said the IPO could still take place before the end of 2026, but an early-2027 debut was considered more likely. "There's confidence a January window is feasible," said one. The bankers are meeting investors in Shanghai, Hong Kong and Beijing ahead of planned marketing in Frankfurt and London. Some Asian investors are also showing renewed interest in more traditional industrial companies as enthusiasm for artificial intelligence-related stocks cools, the sources added. Syngenta, which Sinochem (600500.SS) acquired for $43 billion in 2017, plans to sell a stake of 10% to 20% and use the [USN:L1N3Z10GT TEXT:"proceeds"] to reduce debt and invest in crop-protection products and seeds. The company has already [USN:L4N4570NW TEXT:"filed"] for the flotation which could raise $5 billion to $10 billion. Hong Kong's IPO market is booming, with 118 newly listed companies raising HK$388.0 billion ($49.5 billion) in the first nine months of 2026, up 106% from a year earlier, according to HKEX data. Sentiment weakened this month, however, after a selloff in [USN:L6N46C0R0 TEXT:"AI-related stocks"] raised concerns over valuations and returns on AI spending. Changzhou Microintelligence and Jiangsu Slender West Lake Culture and Tourism [USN:L3N46C0CM TEXT:"postponed"] their offerings, citing [USN:FWN4660V7 TEXT:"market conditions"]. Syngenta's IPO would revive Sinochem's efforts to take the company public after it withdrew a proposed Shanghai listing in 2024. Syngenta competes with BASF (BASFn.DE) , Bayer (BAYGn.DE) and Corteva (CTVA.N) , and recently appointed as CEO Hengde Qin, a Chinese national seen as someone who can navigate the various approval processes. The company sells seeds, herbicides, insecticides and fungicides, alongside biological and digital farming products. It has more than 50,000 employees in over 90 countries, according to its website.

item.title: Safra de soja do Brasil poderia cair 10% em cenário de perdas por El Niño, projeta Serasa
item.description: A safra de soja do Brasil 2026/27 poderia cair para 163,6 milhões de toneladas em cenário de perdas por efeitos do fenômeno climático El Niño forte, uma redução de cerca de 10% no comparativo com uma situação neutra, projetou nesta terça-feira um estudo da Serasa Experian.
item.dc:creator: Roberto Samora
item.content:encoded: A safra de soja do Brasil 2026/27 poderia cair para 163,6 milhões de toneladas em cenário de perdas por efeitos do fenômeno climático El Niño forte, uma redução de cerca de 10% no comparativo com uma situação neutra, projetou nesta terça-feira um estudo da Serasa Experian. A previsão foi feita com base no histórico de ocorrência do El Niño para as áreas de soja do país, maior produtor e exportador global da commodity. Sem as perdas, a safra poderia alcançar 181,2 milhões de toneladas, de acordo com o estudo, que considera um aumento de 900 mil hectares na área plantada (ou 1,8%) em relação ao ciclo anterior, para 49,9 milhões de hectares. A Serasa avalia que regiões produtoras de soja do Centro-Oeste concentrariam as maiores perdas por El Niño, que poderiam somar 9,7 milhões de toneladas em Mato Grosso e 4 milhões de toneladas em Goiás, já que essas áreas poderiam sofrer mais com a falta de chuvas e temperaturas elevadas. O estudo foi divulgado após o plantio da safra de soja do Brasil ter avançado bem em diversas regiões nas últimas semanas, mostrando antecipação em relação ao mesmo período do ano passado, com exceção do Sul do país, onde as chuvas excessivas limitaram os avanços. Segundo dado divulgado na segunda-feira pela AgRural, o país havia plantado [USN:S0N45E02O TEXT:"40%"] da área estimada até a última quinta-feira. Neste momento, disse o gerente de geoprocessamento agro da Serasa Experian, Daniel de Oliveira, o risco do El Niño começa a se "deslocar" da fase de plantio para a fase de desenvolvimento das lavouras. "Quando começa a olhar para regiões relevantes, o risco deixa de ser para a implantação, mas como as chuvas vão ser distribuídas... para que o produtor não enfrente redução da produtividade tal como vimos na 2023/24", disse ele. Ele observou que o produtor aproveitou a segunda quinzena de outubro para implantar a lavoura de soja, trazendo uma situação de "normalidade" para o Mato Grosso. "Mas o risco ainda não desapareceu, ainda não conseguimos dizer que a safra 26/27 está livre dos impactos que a gente está discutindo nesse estudo", afirmou, lembrando que o clima precisa colaborar para o florescimento e a formação de grãos em novembro e dezembro em importantes Estados produtores. Na última ocorrência de El Niño forte, observou a Serasa, citando números da estatal Conab, a produtividade média do Brasil caiu mais de 8% em 2024, para 3.282 kg/hectare, no comparativo com 2023, quando houve uma La Niña fraca. Considerando as perdas previstas na produtividade, o setor poderia ter prejuízo de R$33 bilhões, em número baseado em preços de agosto, apontou a Serasa, ponderando que uma oferta menor tende a elevar as cotações e mexer nas condições de comercialização. Por outro lado, o Rio Grande do Sul poderia colher 5,5 milhões de toneladas a mais, já que o Estado sulista geralmente recebe mais chuvas em anos de El Niño. O pior cenário da Serasa indica que haveria perda de produtividade em 13 Estados brasileiros, enquanto poderia haver ganhos ligeiros em quatro unidades da federação. Além de Mato Grosso e Goiás, a Serasa indicou redução na produtividade no Paraná, São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Mato Grosso do Sul, Bahia, Maranhão, entre outros, no cenário de perdas por El Niño forte.

item.title: Poorer Brazilians devote four times more income to credit card debt, central bank says
item.description: Lower-income Brazilians are devoting an increasing share of their earnings to interest on credit-card- and other high-cost consumer borrowing, prompting policymakers to consider how to reduce excessive debt.
item.dc:creator: Marcela Ayres
item.content:encoded: Lower-income Brazilians are devoting an increasing share of their earnings to interest on credit-card- and other high-cost consumer borrowing, prompting policymakers to consider how to reduce excessive debt. The new central bank data point to a growing reliance on expensive forms of credit since late 2023, in the first year of President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's current term. Lula's administration has long championed greater credit availability as a way to support economic growth. But in its latest financial stability report, the central bank again flagged concern over the rising portion of household budgets absorbed by the servicing of high-interest borrowing and [USN:L1N44L0KT TEXT:"reiterated"] that it was studying macroprudential measures aimed at riskier lending segments. Among borrowers earning up to twice the minimum wage, or 3,242 reais ($604) in total, the share of income being spent on credit card debt stood at 15% in June, close to historical highs and four times the 3.75% recorded among those earning more than 10 times the minimum wage. The gap was also evident in unsecured consumer loans. For borrowers earning up to twice the minimum wage, the share of income committed to servicing that debt stood at 9.6% in June, compared to 3.1% among those earning more than 10 times the minimum wage. The central bank said the [USN:L6N4570VW TEXT:"rapid digitalization"] of financial services had significantly increased the availability of credit offers to lower-income consumers, and thus raised debt levels. "In response, the central bank is considering macroprudential measures targeting higher-risk credit segments to reduce overindebtedness and strengthen credit sustainability and financial system resilience," it said, without providing details. The report said debt-servicing capacity is strained for both households and companies. Among families, debt burdens have reached their highest level in 21 years, with low-income borrowers bearing the brunt. The central bank said credit risk has increased and is likely to remain elevated in the near term. Troubled assets in household lending have risen across most credit segments to their highest levels since 2012, driven primarily by delinquency, while default indicators point to continued pressure through the second half of the year. ($1 = 5.3719 reais)

item.title: High inflation to persist globally into next year, Reuters poll shows
item.description: High inflation will persist in the global economy well into next year, according to hundreds of economists polled by Reuters, who are now increasingly concerned that price pressures will become entrenched beyond rising energy costs caused by the conflict in the Middle East.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: High inflation will persist in the global economy well into next year, according to hundreds of economists polled by Reuters, who are now increasingly concerned that price pressures will become entrenched beyond rising energy costs caused by the conflict in the Middle East. More than $1 trillion of investment in artificial intelligence technology globally since last year has made some economies more resilient at a time when cost of living pressures are squeezing households and shaping national politics. Most central banks have raised interest rates only a few times or not at all, but more could come if inflation pressures broaden. A global rout in bond markets in recent months has also tightened financial conditions through higher yields. Crude oil [USN:L2N46D00J TEXT:"prices"], which have stayed above $100 a barrel since October 7, hit a six-month high of over $117 last week and are up more than 60% since the US-Israeli war with Iran began almost eight months ago. Even forecasters who did not anticipate a quick end to the war are now sounding more concerned about inflation resurgence, particularly given the resilience of global growth. More than 500 economists Reuters surveyed globally this month raised their 2027 inflation forecasts for 31 of the 50 economies polled on and growth forecasts for 23 of them. "I am getting much more concerned about inflation again," said Janet Henry, global chief economist at HSBC. "The longer the situation evolves and escalates in the Middle East and the higher the broad basket of price pressures builds, the greater the likelihood that we get not just higher but more persistent inflation." Economists raised 2027 inflation forecasts for 15 of 21 developed economies covered. That suggests inflation worries are spreading and affecting economies that typically experience low price pressures. Cumulatively, median forecasts for 2027 inflation over the past three quarterly polls have risen by 0.7 percentage points for [USN:L6N4610Q9 TEXT:"Britain"], 0.5 percentage points for the [USN:L6N45U0QU TEXT:"euro zone"] and only 0.2 percentage points so far for the US. They have risen by 0.4 percentage points for India and by 0.5 percentage point for [USN:L6N4650KO TEXT:"Brazil"]. "Higher energy prices continue to ripple through the global economy, but economic activity remains resilient, supported by the AI-led investment cycle and firmer-than-expected activity across several regions," Seth Carpenter, global chief economist at Morgan Stanley, said in a note. "The inflation picture has become more complex as signs of energy pass-through into core measures are beginning to emerge." The effects of rising prices on household budgets have taken centre stage in various political campaigns across the world. Opinion polls show voters ahead of US midterm elections on November 3 are preoccupied with these issues and Brazil's presidential [USN:L2N46B01X TEXT:"election"], which gave incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva his fourth non-consecutive term, was also fought on cost of living issues. In contrast to two previous polls in April and July, which painted a weak-growth, high-inflation scenario, the latest forecasts lean towards one where price pressures accompany more robust economic performance. Economists upgraded their global growth forecasts for both this year and next, to 3.0% and 3.2%, respectively, from 2.9% and 3.1% in the July poll, though the 2027 forecast is lower than the 3.4% the International Monetary Fund is predicting. The US, which [USN:L6N46606V TEXT:"leads"] in AI capital expenditure that has now become the main driver of domestic growth, is forecast to expand 2.3% this year and 2.1% in 2027. ([USN:L6N45N0UX TEXT:"Other stories"] from the Reuters global economic poll)

item.title: Ibovespa segue fragilizado com investidor atento a sinal fiscal após tombo com reeleição de Lula
item.description: A bolsa paulista ensaiou uma acomodação nesta terça-feira, mas o Ibovespa voltava a trabalhar com sinal negativo, um dia depois de forte reprecificação dos ativos brasileiros na véspera, que acionou o "circuit breaker" no pregão, na esteira da reeleição do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.
item.dc:creator: Paula Arend Laier
item.content:encoded: A bolsa paulista ensaiou uma acomodação nesta terça-feira, mas o Ibovespa voltava a trabalhar com sinal negativo, um dia depois de forte reprecificação dos ativos brasileiros na véspera, que acionou o "circuit breaker" no pregão, na esteira da reeleição do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. Por volta de 11h10, o Ibovespa (.BVSP) , referência do mercado acionário brasileiro, recuava 0,82%, a 175.156,77 pontos, tendo alcançado 178.526,08 pontos na máxima até o momento. O volume financeiro no pregão brasileiro somava R$21,57 bilhões. Na segunda-feira, o Ibovespa [USN:S0N450028 TEXT:"caiu"] 13,88%, maior queda desde 2020, uma vez que o desfecho da eleição contrariou expectativas no mercado de vitória do senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e uma possível agenda econômica mais favorável ao ajuste fiscal. De acordo com levantamento da Elos Ayta, o valor de mercado consolidado das empresas listadas na B3 registrou uma queda de R$734 bilhões na segunda-feira. Para o responsável pela área de renda variável da Criteria, Thiago Pedroso, parte da queda da segunda-feira pode ser explicada pelo desmonte acelerado de posições (com o resultado contrariando expectativas), e não necessariamente por uma deterioração equivalente dos fundamentos econômicos. "A preocupação estrutural, entretanto, permanece", afirmou em comentário a clientes no começo desta terça-feira, destacando que o principal desafio do novo mandato será recuperar a credibilidade fiscal. "A trajetória da dívida pública, a rigidez das despesas obrigatórias e a necessidade de resultados primários mais consistentes continuarão limitando o espaço para a redução sustentável dos juros." Em Brasília, o ministro da Fazenda, Dario Durigan, afirmou mais cedo que reafirmou a Lula a necessidade de dar uma [USN:L2N46D0LK TEXT:"sinalização"] propositiva ao mercado e que o governo já tem medidas prontas para apresentação, incluindo a que permite a busca do centro da meta fiscal. DESTAQUES VALE ON (VALE3.SA) recuava 1,55%, em meio ao declínio dos futuros do minério de ferro na China, onde o contrato mais negociado na Bolsa de Mercadorias de Dalian fechou o pregão diurno com queda de 0,9%. Também no radar está o balanço da mineradora do terceiro trimestre, previsto para quinta-feira, após o fechamento do mercado. PETROBRAS PN caía 1,21%, com a fraqueza do petróleo no exterior também no radar. O barril do Brent mostrava queda de 1,29%, a US$114,32. O Goldman Sachs prevê que a Petrobras deverá manter os [USN:L6N46D0VL TEXT:"preços do diesel"] vendido a distribuidoras inalterados até o fim do ano, após o governo brasileiro ter decidido prorrogar por mais 30 dias os subsídios ao combustível. BANCO DO BRASIL ON (BBAS3.SA) subia 0,92%, experimentando uma trégua após fechar com um tombo de mais de 29% na véspera, embora tenha já reduzido o fôlego em relação aos primeiros negócios, quando chegou a avançar 4,8%. BRADESCO PN mostrava decréscimo de 0,75%, ITAÚ UNIBANCO PN perdia 0,98%, BTG PACTUAL UNIT recuava 2,23% e SANTANDER BRASIL UNIT caía 2,24%, com o setor como um todo perdendo força após uma abertura mais positiva. O Citi rebaixou as ações do BB para venda e do Bradesco para neutra, enquanto manteve Itaú e BTG com recomendação de compra. B3 ON (B3SA3.SA) avançava 1,66%, em sessão de ajustes. Na véspera, a ação fechou com um tombo superior a 36,28%, após afundar quase 50% no pior momento. Em Nova York, XP (XP.O) subia 1,6%, também refletindo ajustes após desabar mais de 48% na segunda-feira. Analistas do Citi cortaram a recomendação para ambos os papéis para "neutra", avaliando que juros mais altos e a incerteza fiscal devem continuar pressionando o apetite por risco, as entradas líquidas de recursos, a atividade de negociação e as emissões no mercado de capitais. "Embora a qualidade dos negócios permaneça sólida, vemos um ambiente operacional menos favorável." MAGAZINE LUIZA ON (MGLU3.SA) saltava 7,36%, em dia de correção, após afundar mais de 58% na segunda-feira. TENDA ON (TEND3.SA) subia 5,17%, também com ajustes, assim como DIRECIONAL ON (DIRR3.SA) , com elevação de 3,53%, endossadas ainda por relatório do JPMorgan, que elevou a recomendação de ambos os papéis para "overweight". CURY ON (CURY3.SA) , que também teve upgrade, mostrava acréscimo de 1,11%. Na contramão, MRV&CO ON (MRVE3.SA) recuava 5,5%, CYRELA ON (CYRE3.SA) caía 2,04% e EZTEC ON (EZTC3.SA) , que não faz parte do Ibovespa, perdia 7,68%. O JPMorgan manteve MRV&Co com recomendação neutra, mesma classificação que agora estabeleceu para Cyrela e Eztec -- que eram "overweight". GERDAU PN (GGBR4.SA) caía 1,26%, em pregão negativo no setor, com investidores também analisando o [USN:S0N46906J TEXT:"balanço"] da companhia no terceiro trimestre, com lucro líquido ajustado de R$1,52 bilhão, alta de 39,7% sobre o desempenho obtido no mesmo período do ano passado. O vice-presidente financeiro do grupo, Rafael Japur, disse nesta terça-feira que a principal operação da Gerdau, a América do Norte, deve ter [USN:L2N46D0LH TEXT:"volumes de venda menores"] no quarto trimestre, mas margem de lucro operacional estável ante os três meses imediatamente anteriores.

item.title: JetBlue shares rally after airline flags "disconnect" between earnings and bond rout
item.description: JetBlue Airways extended its early gains to surge 20% on Tuesday, after the airline said there was "a significant disconnect" between its third-quarter earnings and a recent bond sell-off.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: JetBlue Airways (JBLU.O) extended its early gains to surge 20% on Tuesday, after the airline said there was "a significant disconnect" between its third-quarter earnings and a recent bond sell-off. The carrier raised its full-year seat revenue growth forecast to 13.5%-14.5% from 10%-12.5%, banking on strong fares and growth in Fort Lauderdale, but flagged fuel costs as a drag. It also ended the quarter with $2.2 billion in liquidity, including a $600 million undrawn credit facility, and about $7 billion in unencumbered assets — $2.8 billion of which are aircraft and engines, following updated appraisals. "I think there's a significant disconnect between the narrative and the bond market and what our financial results are demonstrating," JetBlue CEO Joanna Geraghty told analysts, pointing to the financial flexibility to bridge to the 2028 EPS goal. JetBlue's TrueBlue senior secured note, a bond backed by the airline's loyalty program, came under heavy selling pressure this month, with the price halving to about $47 and yields surging to distressed levels above 30% as of October 26. The industry's quarter was weighed down by surging fuel prices tied to the ongoing war in Iran, which has forced airlines to take measures such as raising fares, cutting [USN:L4N46813M TEXT:"capacity"] or taking on more debt. The fuel headwinds, along with weather and air traffic control disruptions earlier this year, have wiped away roughly 48% of JetBlue's share value, dropping its valuation to $894.23 million and making it the worst-performing US carrier. "Liquidity and $2.8 billion of aircraft assets could provide runway, but the path to profitability hinges on fuel," analysts at TD Cowen said. Fuel costs surged for JetBlue in the third quarter, with the airline paying $3.91 per gallon, up 57% from a year earlier. By comparison, unit revenue increased 18.4%, highlighting the pressure rising fuel expenses continue to place on margins despite stronger pricing. Short interest in the stock is currently at 25%.

item.title: Artiva to discontinue cell therapy after two patient deaths, cut workforce by 94%
item.description: Artiva Biotherapeutics said on Tuesday it would halt the development of an experimental cell therapy for certain autoimmune conditions — its lead candidate — after two patient deaths, sending its shares slumping 32%.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Artiva Biotherapeutics (ARTV.O) said on Tuesday it would halt the development of an experimental cell therapy for certain autoimmune conditions — its lead candidate — after two patient deaths, sending its shares slumping 32%. The company will slash its workforce by about 94% and evaluate strategic alternatives, it said. Here are more details: Artiva's therapy AlloNK was being tested as a potential treatment for autoimmune conditions such as rheumatoid arthritis in a mid-stage trial The company said one of the patients in the trial experienced a fatal neurological event following treatment The investigator and an independent safety review assessed the event as likely related to complications caused by the chemotherapy drug fludarabine, the company said A second patient in the trial experienced sudden death about two months after initiating treatment, which an investigator assessed as unrelated to AlloNK, Artiva added "Two patient deaths plus fading durability quickly transformed what looked like a promising and differentiated path forward into one that carried too much risk and uncertainty," said Cantor Fitzgerald analyst Josh Schimmer Schimmer said a path forward with AlloNK would have been a challenging one with an incredibly high cost of capital As of September 30, Artiva had about $319.1 million in cash, cash equivalents and investments As of December 31, 2025, the company had 104 full-time employees, according to its annual filing

item.title: BC diz que estuda medidas para conter endividamento com foco em crédito de maior risco
item.description: O Banco Central estuda adotar medidas macroprudenciais voltadas a segmentos de crédito de maior risco, afirmou a autoridade monetária em relatório divulgado nesta terça-feira, citando experiências internacionais de reforço na avaliação sobre a capacidade de pagamento das pessoas que contraem dívidas.
item.dc:creator: Bernardo Caram
item.content:encoded: O Banco Central estuda adotar medidas macroprudenciais voltadas a segmentos de crédito de maior risco, afirmou a autoridade monetária em relatório divulgado nesta terça-feira, citando experiências internacionais de reforço na avaliação sobre a capacidade de pagamento das pessoas que contraem dívidas. Em entrevista à imprensa, o presidente da autarquia, Gabriel Galípolo, ressaltou que a instituição pretende anunciar novas medidas sobre crédito ainda neste ano e destacou preocupação com linhas de financiamento sem garantia. "A gente se debruçou, estudou as experiências internacionais e vem observando que a questão comportamental, de experiência do cliente e de como isso é ofertado têm um peso muito grande nesse processo, são com essas linhas que estamos bastante preocupados e mirando os próximos passos", disse. Na mesma entrevista, o diretor de Fiscalização do BC, Ailton de Aquino, citou preocupação com cartões de crédito e outras linhas de crédito não garantido. Em seu Relatório de Estabilidade Financeira, publicação semestral, a autoridade monetária ressaltou que as medidas em avaliação têm o objetivo de reduzir o superendividamento e fortalecer a sustentabilidade do crédito e a resiliência do sistema financeiro nacional. O BC apontou que pesquisa da autarquia indica que a crescente digitalização dos serviços financeiros tem ampliado significativamente a exposição de consumidores de menor renda a ofertas, contribuindo para intensificar o endividamento, tema que é "fonte relevante de preocupação para o BC e para o mercado financeiro". "Diversos países já utilizam medidas macroprudenciais para mitigar as vulnerabilidades dos tomadores, buscando reforçar a resiliência das famílias ao longo do ciclo financeiro", disse o BC no documento. Segundo a autarquia, nesse processo o desafio é capturar as diferentes dimensões das vulnerabilidades dos tomadores de crédito para subsidiar o desenho de instrumentos adequados. Nesse sentido, uma tendência comum é a crescente incorporação da situação financeira e da capacidade de pagamento dos tomadores ao monitoramento da estabilidade financeira. O presidente do BC, Gabriel Galípolo, tem destacado a preocupação com os níveis de endividamento no país, ressaltando a importância da promoção do uso responsável dos instrumentos de crédito e do devido provisionamento por parte dos bancos. Em agosto já havia afirmado que o BC estava avaliando experiências internacionais de medidas macroprudenciais. A [USN:L1N4650WU TEXT:"Reuters"] mostrou na semana passada que o conjunto de ações em preparação pelo BC começaria por medidas de prevenção e transparência, enquanto a autarquia ainda analisa modelo regulatório que poderá limitar o crédito autorizado por pessoa a depender do nível de renda --sistema usado por Cingapura. O plano foi iniciado três dias depois, quando o BC [USN:L1N46916M TEXT:"aprovou"] três resoluções sobre as responsabilidades de instituições financeiras na oferta e concessão de crédito, com novas salvaguardas contra ofertas inadequadas ou abusivas e maior transparência antes da contratação. Em seu relatório, a autarquia citou avaliação do Fundo Monetário Internacional (FMI) sobre o Brasil na qual a instituição enfatiza que a análise do endividamento das famílias deve ir além da inadimplência e considerar também a capacidade dos tomadores de absorver choques, destacando indicadores como a relação entre o serviço da dívida e a renda da pessoa. "Riscos associados à concessão de crédito incompatível com a situação financeira dos consumidores demonstram a necessidade de ampla coordenação para evitar o superendividamento das famílias", disse. No documento, a autarquia mencionou o sistema de Cingapura, que limita o comprometimento da renda com o serviço da dívida e tem medidas para "restringir o acúmulo excessivo de dívida pelas famílias", bem como modelos de Canadá, Suécia, Coreia do Sul e Nova Zelândia, que têm exigências ou limitações na concessão de crédito. O BC apontou ainda que o apetite a risco das instituições financeiras mostrou sinais de redução no primeiro semestre, quando o financiamento à economia real desacelerou, e a perspectiva é de crédito ainda mais restritivo no segundo semestre. "O ambiente de juros contracionistas, elevado endividamento e maior materialização de risco requer cautela e diligência adicionais na concessão de crédito, tanto na qualidade das operações quanto no apetite ao risco", disse o BC. Segundo a autarquia, a despeito de as incertezas seguirem elevadas, não há risco relevante para a estabilidade financeira no país.

item.title: Boeing share price plummets with slower 737 production and free cash flow growth outlook
item.description: Boeing CEO Kelly Ortberg said on Tuesday that the company will not reach its 737 production rate target of 47 jets a month until early 2027, a serious setback to the company's ongoing recovery. As a result, the company will not hit its delivery target of 500 jets this year.
item.dc:creator: Dan Catchpole, Shivansh Tiwary
item.content:encoded: Boeing (BA.N) CEO Kelly Ortberg said on Tuesday that the company will not reach its 737 production rate target of 47 jets a month until early 2027, a serious setback to the company's ongoing recovery. As a result, the company will not hit its delivery target of 500 jets this year. The company also expects much slower free cash flow growth than investors had expected - $3 billion next year and $6 billion in 2028, compared to Wall Street analysts' consensus projection of $5.6 billion and $9.6 billion, respectively, according to LSEG data. Shares of the US planemaker fell 9.5% in early trading, reaching April 2025 lows, even as Boeing continues to recover from [USN:L2N3OO01G TEXT:"years of crises and controversies"] that dented its reputation, drained cash and saddled it with a heavy debt load. The company had planned to reach 47 737 jets per month [USN:FWN4240QK TEXT:"this past summer"], but it will take "into early next year," Ortberg said during an interview on CNBC. In September, he said that Boeing has not been able to make wings fast enough. Deliveries of the popular single-aisle jetliner are a major driver of Boeing's cash flow. "We are ramping up aircraft, and we're doing that in the right way," he said. Before Ortberg joined Boeing in 2024, the company had struggled for years with production quality problems that were attributed to rushing rate increases at the expense of quality. There is pressure on the company to increase 737 output faster, "but we're going to be smart about this, stay disciplined, and the outlook is there," Ortberg said. The company continues to struggle with production challenges in its 787 program and 777 freighters, as first reported by Reuters on Friday. High fuel prices have kept demand up for more fuel-efficient jetliners, but "certainly something we have to continue to watch," Ortberg said on CNBC. During the quarter, Boeing [USN:L1N4660X2 TEXT:"secured certification"] for the 737 MAX 7 from US regulators, won the US Navy's sixth-generation F/A-XX [USN:L6N45R0R4 TEXT:"fighter contract"] and generated free cash flow for another quarter, while certification of the larger MAX 10 followed in October. "Expectations are rising, and they should. We have a stronger foundation than a year ago, but we also have more work to do to deliver on our backlog, strengthen our culture, and improve how we work every day," Ortberg said in a memo to employees after the results. Boeing reported an adjusted loss of 34 cents per share for the quarter through September, compared with market expectation of 21 cents, according to data compiled by LSEG. Revenue at Boeing Commercial Airplanes dipped slightly to $10.7 billion, while operating loss stood at $697 million and margin shrank by just 6.5% compared with a contraction of 48.3% a year ago. The company attributed the performance to less profitable jetliner deliveries and higher production costs, including from its supply chain. At Boeing's defense division, higher deliveries, improved operational performance and a $252-million sale of a subsidiary contributed to nearly $500 million in quarterly earnings with an operating margin of 6.2%, up from 1.7% a year ago. Boeing Global Services earned $1 billion and posted an operating margin of 18.3%. The US planemaker ended the quarter with $25.2 billion in net debt, down slightly from $25.9 billion in the previous three months and $30.4 billion a year ago.

item.title: Canadian stocks muted as energy losses offset gains in mining, tech
item.description: Canada's main stock index was muted in choppy trading on Tuesday as gains in mining and tech stocks were countered by declining energy shares, while investors awaited crucial monetary policy decisions from central banks due later this week.
item.dc:creator: Anand R
item.content:encoded: Canada's main stock index was muted in choppy trading on Tuesday as gains in mining and tech stocks were countered by declining energy shares, while investors awaited crucial monetary policy decisions from central banks due later this week. The S&P/TSX Composite Index (.GSPTSE) was down 0.1% at 35,897.12 points as of 10:28 a.m. ET (1428 GMT). The materials sector (.GSPTTMT) was the biggest gainer, up 1.3% as copper prices rose and gold reversed declines from earlier in the day Information technology stocks (.SPTTTK) were 0.2% higher, lifted by gains in data center infrastructure firm Celestica (CLS.TO) , though most other tech stocks declined Celestica (CLS.TO) topped the TSX with a 10% jump after [USN:L2N46C109 TEXT:"beating third-quarter"] revenue and profit estimates Energy stocks (.SPTTEN) lost 1.1% after oil prices turned negative, as markets balanced hopes that potential Middle East talks could ease supply disruptions against Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia's infrastructure "Oil prices going higher is a big driver of the energy component of the stock market, but that doesn't mean it's good," said Matt Manara, executive vice president and portfolio manager at Avenue Investment Management Reuters reported, citing sources, that the US and Canada are working on a [USN:L2N46C11U TEXT:"deal to ease US tariffs"] on Canadian steel as the two countries try to repair relations that soured after trade talks broke down in August "If they are able to ease tariffs and markets stay strong, that is good for capital markets, which translates into bank profits, which are 30% of the TSX," said Manara This week, attention will be on the US Federal Reserve's policy meeting, with the central bank widely expected to hold interest rates steady, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool The Bank of Canada meets on Wednesday, with markets pricing in a 78% chance of a 25-basis-point hike, according to data compiled by LSEG On Monday, financials and resources shares helped the TSX stage a rebound, with the latter supported by British Columbia's provincial election result, which raised production prospects for oil and gas companies

item.title: El dólar sube levemente a medida que la atención se centra en reuniones de bancos centrales
item.description: El dólar se fortalecía el martes frente a las principales divisas, entre ellas el euro, el yen y la libra esterlina, en un contexto de posicionamiento del mercado ante una serie de reuniones de los bancos centrales en las que se esperan nuevas pistas sobre las perspectivas económicas y la trayectoria de las tasas de interés.
item.dc:creator: Alun John, Chibuike Oguh
item.content:encoded: El dólar se fortalecía el martes frente a las principales divisas, entre ellas el euro, el yen y la libra esterlina, en un contexto de posicionamiento del mercado ante una serie de reuniones de los bancos centrales en las que se esperan nuevas pistas sobre las perspectivas económicas y la trayectoria de las tasas de interés. * La Reserva Federal tiene previsto anunciar su última decisión de política monetaria el miércoles, el Banco Central Europeo lo hará el jueves y el Banco de Japón cerrará la semana el viernes. * Se espera que los tres mantengan las tasas sin cambios, por lo que la atención se centrará en cualquier indicio que den los responsables a cargo de la política monetaria sobre sus perspectivas. * El dólar también se ha estabilizado tras sufrir presiones a raíz de la ola de ventas que afectó la semana pasada a las acciones de empresas de inteligencia artificial, que venían registrando fuertes subidas. * El euro bajaba un 0,25% frente a la moneda estadounidense, a 1,1144 dólares. * El euro va camino de ser la divisa de los mercados desarrollados con peor comportamiento en octubre, con una caída del 1,65% frente al dólar, lastrado por los elevados costos energéticos, la volatilidad de los bonos del Estado francés y las preocupaciones sobre la situación fiscal de Francia. * La moneda única amplió ligeramente su caída tras la publicación de la Encuesta Trimestral sobre Préstamos Bancarios del BCE, que puso de manifiesto que el impacto de sus subidas de tasas está empezando a hacerse notar. Si esa tendencia continúa, podría, en cierta medida, reducir la presión sobre el BCE para que continúe con las subidas de tasas hasta bien entrado el próximo año. * El yen fue una de las divisas principales con mejor comportamiento la semana pasada, apreciándose alrededor de un 0,75% frente al dólar, su mayor subida semanal desde principios de septiembre, ya que el nerviosismo en torno a la IA en el mercado de valores provocó una fuga hacia la divisa. * El dólar subía un 0,15%, a 157,73 yenes japoneses . La libra esterlina se debilitaba un 0,16% frente al dólar, a 1,3317 dólares. * El índice dólar , que mide la evolución de la moneda estadounidense frente a una cesta de seis divisas que incluye el yen y el euro, subía un 0,2%, a 102,22.

item.title: Who controls powerful AI? Anthropic has a plan for long after its leaders depart
item.description: Few public companies claim to have the future of humanity on the line while making mundane choices about board composition.
item.dc:creator: Jeffrey Dastin, Ross Kerber
item.content:encoded: Few public companies claim to have the future of humanity on the line while making mundane choices about board composition. Not so with Anthropic. Having warned that its artificial intelligence could one day cure cancer or kill up to 8 billion people, Anthropic has set up a complex plan for who can govern the company as its technology rapidly progresses, its [USN:L4N45L0EZ TEXT:"Monday IPO filing showed"]. Its expected [USN:L6N46118I TEXT:"$1.5 trillion valuation"] would make Anthropic the world's most highly valued public benefit corporation, a setup under Delaware law that means the AI lab must balance investor interests with promoting a wider good. More than fine print, Anthropic's setup may have big implications for investors and a public increasingly adopting the San Francisco-based company's AI. The details show how Anthropic has insulated itself from investor pressure so it can pursue what it says is best for humanity. Anthropic gave 50.1% voting power over certain matters to its seven co-founders, who, according to the filing, are "distinctly equipped to be stewards of our mission," [USN:L1N45K0N6 TEXT:"Reuters previously reported"]. Though an independent trust will control a majority of board seats, the co-founders' supervoting power will extend to elections of the remaining directors and shareholder proposals generally. The Monday filing revealed still more intricacies to overseeing a business that Anthropic expects will outlive the tight-knit crew that created it. Once most of its co-founders are out of the picture and their "Class F" supervoting stock is gone, Anthropic's board will divide into three similarly sized groups, serving three-year terms. Staggering directors' reelection like in the US Senate, Anthropic has embraced a structure once popular as a way to stem hostile takeovers. The company has long voiced concern about the risks of AI falling into authoritarian or nefarious hands. That structure also goes against some corporate-governance tides. In this century, major US companies have largely moved to electing all directors annually , making companies more responsive to shareholder demands on areas like executive pay or strategy. Anthropic declined to comment. 'LONG-TERM FLEXIBILITY' Beyond its board, Anthropic has another governing body with its own set of rules: its long-term benefit trust. Currently chaired by global health leader Neil "Buddy" Shah, the trust controls a special share class called "Class T" stock that will let it elect a majority of Anthropic's board. Anthropic has contemplated what happens if that stock goes away, too. The goal of such eventualities is to "preserve long-term flexibility if circumstances change," its filing said. Even if someone not bound by Anthropic's mission to benefit humanity takes hold of its Class T stock, Anthropic's setup would require directors to follow "provisions relating to our public benefit purpose." Ultimately, the trust's power over the board makes Anthropic a "controlled company" under Nasdaq rules, exempting it from following some typical requirements like having an independent nominating and corporate governance committee. Anthropic is using that exemption to put Daniela Amodei, its president and sister of CEO Dario Amodei, on that committee. THE LEADERS IN CHARGE Anthropic set up a safety and risk committee on its board as well, currently made up of Novartis CEO Vas Narasimhan and former Trump White House official Chris Liddell. Billionaire Netflix co-founder Reed Hastings is Anthropic's current lead independent director. Still, Anthropic's seven co-founders — the Amodei siblings among them — remain at the core of governance for the foreseeable future. This partly is through the existence of an entity called "Founder LLC," which, after the trust, will have the biggest say in board elections.

item.title: Centene lifts 2026 profit forecast, sees earnings growth continuing in 2027
item.description: Centene raised its annual profit forecast and said it expects 2027 earnings to be higher than this year, sending the health insurer's shares up 3%.
item.dc:creator: Sneha K, Padmanabhan Ananthan
item.content:encoded: Centene (CNC.N) raised its annual profit forecast and said it expects 2027 earnings to be higher than this year, sending the health insurer's shares up 3%. Higher medical costs in recent years due to elevated healthcare demand have squeezed margins for health insurers and prompted them to improve pricing and tighten cost controls. Centene has made great progress managing cost trends and improving its cost structure, CEO Sarah London said on a post-earnings call. The company expects 2027 earnings to grow from both its updated baseline of $4.70 per share and its raised 2026 adjusted profit forecast of more than $5.20 per share. Analysts expect a profit of $5.34 per share for 2027, as per data compiled by LSEG. "Investors may appreciate the positive expected growth trajectory, despite the uncertainty around the important Medicaid market next year," said Morningstar analyst Julie Utterback. The company has been facing Medicaid enrollment losses due to stricter eligibility rules, which have pushed some beneficiaries off coverage rolls, leaving insurers with a relatively sicker population that requires more medical care. States are opting for a more methodical approach to eligibility verifications, which should smooth membership impacts across 2027 and into early 2028, Centene said. Centene said costs in its Medicaid plans for low-income individuals were in line with its expectations, in part due to higher reimbursement rates from states. The company also said it was on track to breakeven in its Medicare Advantage business in 2026, a year ahead of expectations. COSTS IN CHECK Centene lowered its forecast for full-year medical cost ratio, a measure of premiums spent on medical care, to 90.4% to 91.1%, from 90.5% to 91.3% previously. Its third-quarter medical cost ratio of 92.7%, which remained the same as last quarter, was also better than its expectations. Analysts had expected a ratio of 92.84%. The company benefited from improved pricing in its Obamacare plans, established under former President Barack Obama's Affordable Care Act, as well as better performance in its Medicare Advantage plans for older Americans. Centene earned third-quarter adjusted profit of 58 cents per share, higher than analysts' estimate of 10 cents.

item.title: UPS CEO says delivery company will make more money on slightly fewer holiday deliveries
item.description: United Parcel Service raised its annual revenue and profit forecasts on Tuesday on better-than-expected third-quarter earnings after cutting doorstep deliveries of millions of unprofitable packages for Amazon.
item.dc:creator: Nandan Mandayam, Lisa Baertlein
item.content:encoded: United Parcel Service (UPS.N) raised its annual revenue and profit forecasts on Tuesday on better-than-expected third-quarter earnings after cutting doorstep deliveries of millions of unprofitable packages for Amazon. CEO Carol Tome said UPS' focus on more lucrative business means it can make more money delivering slightly fewer packages during its critical peak holiday season quarter every year. Shares of the world's largest parcel delivery firm jumped nearly 3% in early trading. Atlanta-based UPS expects total average daily volume to be down 1.3% in the fourth quarter as it becomes more selective in which packages it delivers. At the same time, executives forecast a roughly 3% rise in revenue in the company's domestic operation, its largest, and an estimated 7% increase in international revenue. "We're dispelling the old belief that all packages were created equal and that volume solves all problems," Tome told Reuters. A widening gap between the cost per parcel and revenue per parcel will improve margins, Chief Financial Officer Brian Dykes said. UPS' reduction in unprofitable deliveries — and the resulting lower volume reduction — in the fourth quarter means UPS can spend less on labor as well as truck and plane leases to handle the holiday package surge, Dykes said. Tome said the outlook for holiday delivery demand is strong as US consumers continue spending despite pressures from rising inflation and prices at the pump. "US consumers remain resilient," she said. SLIMMER OPERATION SETS STAGE FOR GROWTH UPS has shuttered facilities and shed thousands of jobs after scaling back deliveries for Amazon (AMZN.O) , its largest customer. UPS said it completed the Amazon scale-down in the second quarter. Rival FedEx (FDX.N) , which reports results on Wednesday, is using a similar strategy. Both companies have been under pressure from investors to improve margins by focusing on higher-value shipments. Tome also said data center construction is a significant opportunity as it touches every part of UPS, which can fly in critical components such as microprocessors, arrange ocean shipments of equipment, store goods and make final deliveries. For the third quarter, UPS posted adjusted profit of $1.69 per share, lower than $1.74 per share a year ago but above analysts' average estimate of $1.63. Third-quarter adjusted operating margin in UPS' domestic unit, which generates about 65% of company revenue, rose to 7% from 6.4% a year earlier. The smaller but more profitable international package division also reported a higher adjusted operating margin of 14.9% for the third quarter, compared with 14.8% last year. Jefferies analysts said third-quarter earnings showcased a "quarter of strong execution," while Evercore ISI analyst Jonathan Chappell wrote in a note that the results give "some confidence in durability." UPS also said it was on track to meet its target of $3 billion in cost savings this year. It has saved $1.8 billion through September. The company now expects 2026 adjusted profit of around $7.28 per share, compared with the $7.22 it had forecast in July. Analysts expect the company to report a profit of $7.19 per share, according to data compiled by LSEG. UPS expects annual revenue of $92.6 billion, compared with its previous projection of $91.2 billion and above analysts' estimate of $91.73 billion.

item.title: Last Republican incumbent senator in a Democratic-leaning state fights for survival
item.description: If Republican Senator Susan Collins wins this nail-biter of an election, it may well be because voters in Maine decide she is not Republican enough.
item.dc:creator: Andy Sullivan
item.content:encoded: If Republican Senator Susan Collins wins this nail-biter of an election, it may well be because voters in Maine decide she is not Republican enough. Since her first victory in 1996, Collins’ reputation as an independent-minded moderate has helped her win reelection even as Maine backed Democrats for president. Now the only Republican incumbent running in a Democratic-leaning state, she is deadlocked in opinion polls with Democrat Troy Jackson in a race that could help determine control of the US Senate. Democrats need a net gain of four seats to take control of the 100-seat Senate from Republicans in the November 3 midterm elections . Jackson, a rough-hewn former logger and state Senate president, has attacked Collins as a rubber stamp for Republican President Donald Trump . Collins is countering with the clout she has amassed over her 30-year Senate career, highlighting projects she has funded and carve-outs she has secured to lessen the [USN:L1N4680R7 TEXT:"economic fallout"] from Trump’s spending cuts, tariffs and war with Iran. “If it wasn't Susan Collins, this race would have been over three months ago,” said Maine Democratic consultant Toby McGrath.
