But strategists in both parties say the pool of the independent-minded, persuadable voters who backed Collins in previous elections has shrunk as partisan lines have hardened and Trump has galvanized Democrats in opposition. “If you hate Trump, you're voting for whoever the Democrats put on the ballot,” said Phil Harriman, a former Republican state senator. Democrats faced a potential debacle this summer, when Graham Platner, an oyster farmer and Marine veteran, won the party’s nomination [USN:S0N42B09J TEXT:"only to drop out"] after facing a rape accusation that he denied. The party quickly united behind Jackson, who has invoked his hardscrabble upbringing in the remote logging town of Allagash as he campaigns on a populist agenda of universal healthcare and raising taxes on the wealthy. “I saw at a young age how people with money and power and influence can hold people back,” he said at a campaign event on Saturday. $1.5 BILLION IN EARMARKS In recent weeks, Collins has visited projects she has funded through her work on the powerful Senate Appropriations Committee: a wastewater treatment plant in North Windham, a dock in Bucksport, an emergency center in Farmington. She says she has secured nearly $1.5 billion in earmarks since 2021. “This has required hard work, knowledge and seniority. The question for voters in this campaign is who can do more for Maine,” she said at an October 15 debate. That influence, she argues, has also helped to shield Maine from the Trump administration’s policies. As Trump’s [USN:L6N4580Y1 TEXT:"trade war with Canada"] has hammered the state’s economy, Collins has pointed to tariff exemptions the administration has granted at her request for road salt, cement and equipment used by the state’s blueberry, potato and apple growers. The Trump administration also credited her when it released home-heating oil reserves to try to drive down prices that have increased more than 70% since last year – a [USN:L6N461155 TEXT:"crucial issue"] in a state where roughly half of households rely on the product. Collins has also pointed to a $50 billion fund she crafted to help [USN:L6N3S70P7 TEXT:"rural hospitals"] cope with healthcare cuts in the 2025 tax and spending package that enacted most of Trump’s legislative agenda, as well as money for body-worn cameras and de-escalation training for federal immigration agents following the January killing of two US citizens in Minnesota. 'THERE SHOULDN'T BE A LIST' Jackson argues that these carve-outs amount to little when weighed against the damage caused by Trump. Body cameras and de-escalation training did not stop an immigration agent from [USN:L6N43H0SA TEXT:"killing a state resident"] in July, he says, and residents would not be struggling to heat their homes if Trump had not started the war with Iran, which has pushed up oil prices globally. Trump’s trade war with Canada, he argues, is only possible because Republicans in Congress have surrendered their authority over tariffs to Trump. “I can't believe that the most powerful US senator in the world would stand there and say, 'Well, I got this and this and that off the list,' instead of the fact that there shouldn’t be a list,” he said on Saturday. SIX ADS IN A ROW Meanwhile, a relentless ad war has played out over the state’s airwaves. AdImpact, an analysis firm, estimates $199 million will be spent on the race – equal to $170 for every adult in the state. During a local newscast on Friday, six ads in a row were devoted to the contest. Those ads are chasing a small slice of undecided voters. Democratic activists say they are encountering relatively few people who have yet to decide on a candidate as they campaign door-to-door in Windham, a Portland suburb that backed Collins by a 14-point margin in 2020, even as it backed Democrat Joe Biden over Trump for president. “There’s just a lot less of that persuadable middle than we historically see,” said volunteer Austin Coco. Windham resident Jim Tabor, a retired optician, said he has grown disillusioned with the Republican Party under Trump. A Collins supporter in past elections, he said this year he will back Jackson. “If he turns out to be a bum, I’ll vote against him next time. But Susan Collins won’t be there,” he said.

item.title: Big Tech earnings to test AI boom amid market turmoil
item.description: Amazon , Microsoft and Alphabet are expected to report accelerating cloud growth this week, but turbulence in global markets and mounting concerns over the cost of financing AI investments are clouding the outlook.
item.dc:creator: Aditya Soni
item.content:encoded: Amazon (AMZN.O) , Microsoft (MSFT.O) and Alphabet (GOOGL.O) are expected to report accelerating cloud growth this week, but turbulence in global markets and mounting concerns over the cost of financing AI investments are clouding the outlook. Investors are pressing for evidence that the AI boom can deliver swift returns to justify its enormous price tag. Rising bond yields at AI cloud providers such as CoreWeave (CRWV.O) and record costs to insure Meta Platform's (META.O) debt have amplified concerns about how the massive AI infrastructure buildout is being funded, particularly as higher US interest rates loom. Market turmoil has rekindled warnings of an AI bubble from investors, including hedge fund Citadel's founder Ken Griffin, and pushed companies [USN:L6N46216E TEXT:"to delay their IPOs"]. An expected Democratic sweep of the US midterm elections could spell more trouble for data centers that are already a target of protests over their impact on power grids, electricity bills and the environment. China's [USN:L4N4601U6 TEXT:"tech-stock boom has unravelled"], wiping out about $480 billion in market value in less than four months as concerns over AI demand and spending and Chinese export curbs deflate lofty valuations. The rout could be a warning for global markets. Big Tech's results this week will be a litmus test for AI adoption and economic viability. These three companies — with nearly $1.7 trillion in combined backlog — plan to spend as much as $600 billion this year. Meta's results last week showed just how unforgiving the calculus has become. Better-than-expected revenue growth and an upbeat outlook were overshadowed by increased spending plans, sending its shares down nearly 7% the following day. They are now down more than 4% this year. "The appetite for capital expenditure alone is slowing rapidly," said Brian Mulberry, chief market strategist at Zacks Investment Management. "For Amazon, Google and Microsoft specifically the growth in their cloud companies is a very important line item that will signal if further growth in capital expenditure can be funded without further risks of contracting free cash flow." While the trio's stocks have outperformed ad-driven Meta this year, with gains ranging from 1.2% to 10.1%, they continue to lag behind the S&P 500's near 12% rise. Google Cloud is expected to again lead the three major players in the September quarter, with revenue surging 95.1% to $29.57 billion, according to LSEG data. That would be faster than the 81.8% growth in the previous quarter. Amazon Web Services, the market leader in cloud, is expected to post 38.2% revenue growth on Thursday, up from 36.8% in the previous quarter. Microsoft Azure is expected to expand 47.7%, accelerating from 42% three months earlier, according to Visible Alpha data. Alphabet and Amazon are expected to burn cash for the second and third consecutive quarters, respectively, while Microsoft will likely generate more than $8 billion in cash flow. GOOGLE CLOUD SUCCESS, SEARCH CONCERNS Alphabet's cloud business and in-house chips have emerged as a bright spot in its AI push amid concerns Google's models are falling behind those of OpenAI and Anthropic. But competition from personal AI agents such as Meta's Muse as well as chatbots such as ChatGPT has raised concerns about the search business that has long powered its earnings. Google search revenue growth is expected to slow to 14.7% from 16.8% in the previous quarter, even as total revenue is expected to rise at a slightly faster pace of 25.2% to $128.18 billion. "This quarter, we believe commentary is equally important to quantitative results as competition for search is growing again with agents while there is increased consternation around the payback of AI capital expenditure," Citizens analyst Andrew Boone said. MICROSOFT CHANGES REPORTING SEGMENTS Microsoft will report under a revamped structure for the first time on Wednesday, combining cloud, AI and business software into a division called "Agents and Infra", and Windows, gaming and ad sales into another dubbed "Devices and Consumer". A notable change will be the disclosure of Azure's quarterly revenue, resolving investor frustration over its previous focus on growth rates without absolute figures. Analysts expect Azure to post sales of $33.06 billion in the quarter, powering a 16.7% rise in Microsoft's total revenue to $90.66 billion, slightly slower growth than the previous period. Amazon's overall revenue growth is expected to slow to 12.3% from 19.6% in the previous quarter.

item.title: World to add less clean energy capacity this year, renewables agency chief says
item.description: The world will add less clean energy capacity in 2026 for the first time in five years due to inadequate transmission networks and trade barriers, the chief of the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA) said.
item.dc:creator: Sudarshan Varadhan
item.content:encoded: The world will add less clean energy capacity in 2026 for the first time in five years due to inadequate transmission networks and trade barriers, the chief of the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA) said. Growth in solar and wind capacity has been accelerating every year since 2021, when the coronavirus pandemic disrupted global supply chains. Clean power installations including hydropower surged a record 692 gigawatts, or 15.5%, to 5,149 GW in 2025 — representing half the world's power capacity. Governments have pledged to boost clean energy use to ensure reliable power supply and cut costs, particularly after the US-Israeli war with Iran choked energy supplies and inflated prices. But IRENA Director-General Francesco La Camera noted that there has been a slowdown in renewables deployment in China due to curtailment — or rejection of clean power when a grid hits its limits. "The main cause of a lack of new record in additions this year is the mismatch between generation capacity and the capacity to distribute and transmit electricity," he told Reuters on the sidelines of the Singapore International Energy Week conference. China, the world's biggest renewable energy producer, turned away enough clean energy to power Mexico for a year in the first half of 2026, while networks in nations such as Australia and Japan also failed to keep pace with a surging renewables buildout. "The amount of the (capacity) increase in the other parts of the world this year, I don't think it will offset the slowing down in China," La Camera said. He declined to provide a numerical forecast for expected growth in clean energy additions this year. Renewable energy additions are crucial to reducing global emissions, and the United Nations said in a report last week that "urgent and stringent" emission cuts were required to slow global warming.

item.title: Football Accusé d'avoir offensé la Chine, Mbappé s'excuse mais perd plusieurs partenaires chinois
item.description: Kylian Mbappé, lâché par plusieurs entreprises chinoises après des propos polémiques sur le "dictateur" Mao Zedong, a tenté mardi d'éteindre l'incendie en présentant ses excuses et en marquant son "profond respect pour le peuple chinois et son histoire".
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Kylian Mbappé, lâché par plusieurs entreprises chinoises après des propos polémiques sur le "dictateur" Mao Zedong, a tenté mardi d'éteindre l'incendie en présentant ses excuses et en marquant son "profond respect pour le peuple chinois et son histoire". Dans une vidéo apparue en ligne lundi, on entend l'international français expliquer que le "mème" - une image ou une vidéo, souvent parodique, reprise massivement sur internet - le plus drôle qu'il ait vu de lui-même était celui où son visage avait été greffé sur celui d'"un dictateur chinois". A savoir l'ancien dirigeant chinois Mao Zedong. Les fans multiplient les mèmes superposant le visage du Madrilène à ceux de dirigeants militaires et politiques, suggérant son supposé autoritarisme. Fondateur de la République populaire de Chine, Mao Zedong est perçu par nombre de Chinois comme le sauveur de la nation et les plaisanteries à son sujet sont considérées comme un tabou. Il est mort en 1976. "Lors d'une récente interview, j'ai réagi à une image de moi me mettant en scène. Ce propos était maladroit, et je comprends aujourd'hui qu'il a blessé de nombreuses personnes en Chine et au sein de la communauté chinoise à travers le monde", déclare l'attaquant du Real Madrid dans un communiqué en français, chinois, et anglais. "Je présente mes excuses à toutes celles et ceux que mes mots ont heurtés. Ce n'était absolument pas mon intention. J'ai un profond respect pour le peuple chinois et son histoire, et je suis sincèrement désolé", ajoute-t-il. Dans un entretien accordé le mois dernier à L'Équipe, le Tricolore avait estimé que si certains aspects de cette tendance relevaient du simple divertissement, les mèmes viraux le présentant en dictateur traduisaient "un manque de conscience politique et humaine chez les gens". La controverse autour de la figure de Mao Zedong a pris une telle ampleur que plusieurs partenaires chinois du sportif ont manifesté leur réprobation en rompant avec lui. Ainsi Eastroc Beverage, qui utilisait l'image de Kylian Mbappé sur ses boissons, a déclaré sur le réseau social chinois Weibo s'opposer fermement à tout "comportement qui heurte les sentiments nationaux". "À compter de ce jour, nous mettons fin à toute coopération avec Kylian Mbappé", a ajouté la marque, avant le communiqué d'excuses du footballeur. Les groupes laitiers Mengniu et Milkground ont eux aussi mis fin à leur partenariat avec l'attaquant français. "MALAISE ET OFFENSE" Interrogé sur l'affaire, un porte-parole du ministère chinois des Affaires étrangères a indiqué que les paroles et actes portant atteinte aux sentiments du peuple chinois "se heurteront naturellement à un rejet commun de l'ensemble de la société". La télévision d'État chinoise a suspendu la diffusion de tous les matches et événements impliquant la Liga et Kylian Mbappé. Les publicités dans lesquelles apparaît le joueur ont également été retirées, a rapporté mardi The Paper, un média public chinois. "De la part de la Liga, nous regrettons profondément les déclarations de Kylian Mbappé qui ont provoqué malaise et offense en Chine. Nous comprenons le tort causé et, au nom de la Liga, je souhaite présenter nos sincères excuses au peuple chinois", a déclaré Javier Tebas, le président de la Liga, sur le réseau social X. "Depuis de nombreuses années, nous avons construit une relation de respect, de confiance et de coopération avec la Chine, ses autorités, ses institutions sportives, ses opérateurs audiovisuels et des millions de fans du football espagnol." "Nous ne pouvons pas permettre qu'une action individuelle ternisse cette relation ou nuise aux plus de 20 clubs engagés dans nos compétitions professionnelles et aux millions de supporters chinois", a-t-il précisé, ajoutant que la Liga prenait "toutes les mesures à [sa] portée". La chaîne de télévision publique CCTV a déclaré qu'elle écouterait ce que Kylian Mbappé a à dire après ses excuses et, "plus important encore", observerait ce qu'il ferait. "Nous espérons que la Liga, le Real Madrid et Mbappé lui-même tireront véritablement les leçons de cet épisode, présenteront des excuses sincères et corrigeront en profondeur leurs erreurs", a-t-elle indiqué dans un communiqué. La marque suisse On, dont il est l'ambassadeur depuis le mois dernier, a dit "[prendre] acte avec satisfaction des excuses de Kylian Mbappé". "Nous avons un profond respect pour le peuple chinois et le riche patrimoine culturel de la Chine. Nous restons en dialogue avec nos partenaires et n'avons pas d'autre commentaire à faire pour le moment", a-t-elle ajouté.

item.title: Mbappe seeks to defuse China anger after 'ill-judged' Mao comments
item.description: France soccer captain Kylian Mbappe apologised to China on Tuesday after a fierce backlash over his comments referring to late Chinese leader Mao Zedong as a dictator, underscoring how swiftly global celebrities can come unstuck.
item.dc:creator: Casey Hall, Clare Jim
item.content:encoded: France soccer captain Kylian Mbappe apologised to China on Tuesday after a fierce backlash over his comments referring to late Chinese leader Mao Zedong as a dictator, underscoring how swiftly global celebrities can come unstuck. In a video on a French podcast that has since been taken down, Mbappe is heard discussing a funny meme where his face had been photoshopped on to that of "some guy — I think he's a Chinese dictator". "During a recent interview, I reacted to an image of myself," Real Madrid forward Mbappe said in a statement. "My comment was ill-judged, and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world. "I apologise to everyone my words have upset," added Mbappe, who has ties with firms including Swiss sportswear brand On Holding (49G.BN) , hotel chain Accor (ACCP.PA) and Lego. "This was absolutely not my intention" The backlash highlighted the risks for athletes and brands in the lucrative China market, where satire about Mao, modern China's founding leader who ruled the country from 1949 until his death in 1976, remain a social taboo. Other major organisations that have incurred the wrath of Beijing and Chinese netizens include fashion brand Dolce & Gabbana, Swiss watchmaker Swatch and the National Basketball Association. Some recovered quickly while others took years. "Mbappe's team knew, or should have known, what the true cost of Chinese brand endorsements was all about," said Terrence Burns, sports sponsorship expert and CEO of the T. Burns Sports Group. Swiss-based On Holding, which [USN:L4N45A12B TEXT:"signed Mbappe"] in September after he had spent two decades at US rival Nike, welcomed his apology and said it had "deep respect" for China. Accor did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Denmark's Lego, which has a Mbappe building set on sale in China, said it could not comment. The Mbappe set still featured on Lego's Chinese website on Tuesday. 'WHAT DID HE SAY?' Chinese state media outlet China Daily said Mbappe's remark had "triggered a backlash among his Chinese fans, threatened his lucrative commercial relationships and offered a sharp reminder of the limits of celebrity influence". "What did he say? Many Chinese would rather not repeat it," the state-backed Global Times added. "The message from Chinese consumers is clear: Respect is not optional; one doesn't get to profit from China while disrespecting it. Not a chance." On Chinese social media platform Weibo one user wrote about the apology; "Not accepted. Not forgiven!!". State broadcaster CCTV struck a more conciliatory tone, however,saying it would listen to what Mbappe had to say after his apology, and "even more importantly" watch what he does. "We hope La Liga, Real Madrid, and Mbappe himself will genuinely learn a lesson from this, offer a sincere apology, and thoroughly correct their mistakes," CCTV said in a statement. Real Madrid declined to comment. Brands including dairy companies Mengniu (2319.HK) and Shanghai Milkground Food Tech (600882.SS) as well as Eastroc Beverage (605499.SS) said they were ceasing all cooperation with Mbappe effective immediately. The companies said they "firmly oppose and have zero tolerance for any words or actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people." China's state television has halted broadcasts of all matches and events involving LaLiga and Mbappe, and all advertisements involving Mbappe have been removed, state-backed media outlet the Paper reported on Tuesday. Spain's LaLiga President Javier Tebas issued an apology on X and said his organisation deeply regretted the alleged comments that have caused discomfort and offence in China. "We are taking the measures within our reach and working directly with our partners and interlocutors in China to overcome this situation," Tebas wrote. "A relationship built over so many years cannot be damaged by a single episode." TRENDING ON WEIBO As of 0700 GMT, four topics related to Mbappe were still among the top 10 trending searches on Weibo. Some netizens called for China to blacklist Mbappe and reduce his commercial value to zero. These comments received hundreds of likes. Fans have been creating memes superimposing Mbappe's face on images of military and political leaders to suggest that he has the power to influence decisions at the teams he plays for. Mbappe has been nicknamed "the dictator" in the European press. "In attempting to laugh at himself and his reputation of being a dictator in the locker room, he apparently crossed a red line he didn't know was there," said Brian Jacobsen, chief economic strategist at Annex Wealth Management. In an interview with L'Equipe last month, Mbappe said that although aspects of the meme trend were harmless fun, the viral ones depicting him as a dictator showed "a lack of political and human awareness". A spokesperson for China's Foreign Ministry said words and actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people "will naturally be met with joint opposition from all sectors of Chinese society".

item.title: Two men charged in UK over RAF Fairford incident allegedly linked to Iran
item.description: Two men appeared in a London court on Tuesday charged under Britain's National Security Act following last month's security incident at the RAF Fairford military base, with prosecutors alleging one tried to assist Iranian intelligence in Britain.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Two men appeared in a London court on Tuesday charged under Britain's National Security Act following last month's security incident at the RAF Fairford military base, with prosecutors alleging one tried to assist Iranian intelligence in Britain. [USN:L1N45R08W TEXT:"RAF Fairford"] had been used by US bombers to carry out strikes on Iran, but they [USN:L1N45R04X TEXT:"were withdrawn"] on security grounds shortly after five British men were arrested outside the base in southwest England in the early hours of September 27. The circumstances of the incident, which remain largely unexplained, attracted huge international attention, coming at a time of heightened concern about the security implications for Western states of the war between the United States and Iran. Prime Minister Andy Burnham said earlier this month that the activity at RAF Fairford was likely to have been [USN:L8N45Y178 TEXT:"coordinated in Iran"], which [USN:S8N44X01J TEXT:"Tehran's ambassador to Britain"] has denied. British national Mohmed Abdulkarim, 24, was charged with engaging in conduct that was likely to materially assist a foreign intelligence service between August 31 and September 28. Abdulkarim appeared at Westminster Magistrates' Court alongside Nouman Essghir, a 24-year-old dual British-Iranian national who was first arrested outside RAF Fairford on September 27 and is charged with entering a prohibited place for a purpose prejudicial to the UK on August 22. SUSPECT CALLED POLICE Prosecutors said Abdulkarim, who was in a wheelchair in court, arranged for five men to take three vans and drive to RAF Fairford at the behest of a man called "Ali". The five men bought around £300 ($400) worth of petrol, which was stored in drums, prosecutor Louise Gray said. "One of them was told there was a bomb in the van ... (and) one of them called 999," Gray added, with police arriving shortly after. Gray said Essghir had conducted reconnaissance of the base on instructions from "Ali" in August, adding that he was also in one of the vans which drove to RAF Fairford the following month. After the five men were told there was a bomb, Gray said Essghir sent a message to "Ali" asking "wtf (what the fuck) is going on" but received no reply. Abdulkarim was granted bail ahead of his next court appearance in November. Essghir has been remanded in custody. Police said that six other people, four of whom are British nationals who were arrested outside RAF Fairford on September 27, remain on police bail. The decision to bail suspects after an apparent major incident had drawn scrutiny, but on Tuesday police said that decision had helped secure charges against the two men. ($1 = 0.7505 pounds)

item.title: GSK to nearly double cancer medicines in clinical trials next year
item.description: GSK said on Tuesday that it expects to almost double the number of cancer medicines it has in clinical trials next year, including those in early-stage studies, as it tries to rebuild its oncology business.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: GSK (GSK.L) said on Tuesday that it expects to almost double the number of cancer medicines it has in clinical trials next year, including those in early-stage studies, as it tries to rebuild its oncology business. The drugmaker's clinical-stage portfolio of about 15 assets would likely "come close to doubling" in 2027, Hesham Abdullah, who heads GSK's oncology research and development, told the Wall Street Journal earlier on Tuesday. The British drugmaker has bet big on cancer drugs under CEO Luke Miels, including its $10.6 billion takeover of US biotech [USN:L6N42H0CS TEXT:"Nuvalent"] earlier this year. One of the drugs acquired in the process received approval in July while a regulatory decision on another is expected by November. Miels faces the task of reassuring investors that the company can navigate looming patent cliffs for its blockbuster HIV drugs. "We may have close to 20 phase threes ongoing in 2027," Eric Richards, who heads oncology product development at GSK, told Reuters earlier in the week at a medical meeting. Cancer drugs such as ris-rez and mo-rez are at the centre of GSK's ambitions. On Monday, data from GSK and Hansoh's ris-rez showed that it helped patients with a hard-to-treat cancer live longer without the disease worsening. Five late-stage studies for mo-rez are ongoing as are two of four planned late-stage trials for ris-rez. Cancer drugs contributed £1.08 billion ($1.44 billion) to GSK's first-half sales. The company is due to report third-quarter earnings on Wednesday. ($1 = 0.75 pounds)

item.title: Seoul shantytown fire largely extinguished, Yonhap reports
item.description: A fire that broke out on Tuesday in Guryong village, a shantytown in Seoul's upmarket Gangnam district, affecting 77 households and 107 people, has been largely extinguished, South Korea's Yonhap news agency said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A fire that broke out on Tuesday in Guryong village, a shantytown in Seoul's upmarket Gangnam district, affecting 77 households and 107 people, has been largely extinguished, South Korea's Yonhap news agency said. The main fire was brought under control after 7-1/2 hours, with one woman suffering a minor leg injury, it added. Yonhap said people had evacuated to an emergency shelter. The fire agency deployed 232 personnel and 70 vehicles to fight the blaze, which began at about 3:50 p.m. local time (0650 GMT) in a temporary structure, Yonhap said. Six helicopters were sent to stop it spreading to a nearby mountain. Guryong, often described as Seoul's largest remaining shantytown, emerged in the 1970s and 1980s when families displaced by public works projects settled on the edge of Gangnam without permits. Its densely packed homes are built with flammable materials such as vinyl sheets and plywood. A [USN:L1N3YH00Q TEXT:"major fire"] in the village in January forced hundreds of residents to evacuate.

item.title: Israël Forte participation aux législatives, Netanyahu appelle ses partisans à se mobiliser
item.description: Les quelque 7,3 millions d'électeurs israéliens se pressaient mardi aux urnes pour décider du sort du Premier ministre sortant Benjamin Netanyahu lors des élections législatives, premier scrutin national depuis le choc des attaques meurtrières du Hamas le 7 octobre 2023.
item.dc:creator: Steven Scheer, Pesha Magid
item.content:encoded: Les quelque 7,3 millions d'électeurs israéliens se pressaient mardi aux urnes pour décider du sort du Premier ministre sortant Benjamin Netanyahu lors [USN:L6N46C0PJ TEXT:"des élections législatives"], premier scrutin national depuis le choc des attaques meurtrières du Hamas le 7 octobre 2023. Selon la Commission électorale, 44,9% des électeurs inscrits avaient voté dans les sept premières heures du scrutin. Le taux de participation à 14h00 "a battu tous les records", a déclaré la Commission alors que de longues files se sont formées devant les bureaux de vote, qui ont ouvert à 07h00 heure locale (05h00 GMT) et fermeront à 22h00. Vivement critiqué pour n'avoir pu empêcher l'attaque du 7-Octobre, qui a fait plus de 1.200 morts en Israël et conduit l'Etat hébreu à déclencher des guerres à Gaza, au Liban et en Iran, Benjamin Netanyahu, 77 ans, aborde le scrutin affaibli, malgré le soutien affiché du président américain Donald Trump. Ce test électoral a de fait valeur de référendum après le traumatisme du 7-octobre, mais "Bibi", poursuivi par ailleurs pour des faits de corruption, ambitionne de maintenir son record de longévité au pouvoir après 19 années de mandat cumulées (1996-1999, 2009-2021, depuis 2022). Il doit compter avec la concurrence inattendue de l'ancien chef d'état-major de l'armée israélienne [USN:L8N4690LP TEXT:"Gadi Eisenkot"], 66 ans, qui a promis de diligenter une commission d'enquête publique sur les failles présumées de l'appareil sécuritaire israélien le 7 octobre 2023. Selon les derniers sondages en date, le parti du chef du gouvernement sortant, le Likoud (classé à droite), est au coude-à-coude avec le parti centriste Yashar du général à la retraite. Dans un message adressé à ses partisans plus de cinq heures après l'ouverture des bureaux de vote, Benjamin Netanyahou a exhorté les Israéliens à voter, affirmant que le taux de participation était élevé chez ses adversaires. "Il faut que le nôtre soit élevé lui aussi. Vous devez tous vous rendre en masse aux urnes", a-t-il déclaré. "C'est un moment décisif." L'INCONNUE EISENKOT Durant la campagne, [USN:L8N46017Y TEXT:"Benjamin Netanyahu"], qui réfute toute responsabilité dans l'échec sécuritaire du 7-Octobre, s'est posé en garant de la sécurité d'Israël malgré son isolement sur la scène internationale et s'est prévalu du soutien exclusif de Donald Trump face à la "menace existentielle" de l'Iran, pays contre lequel il entend "finir le travail". "Je pense que ces élections sont les plus importantes de toutes celles que j’ai connues", témoigne Ruth Epstein, une électrice de gauche de 81 ans résidant à Ramat Gan, près de Tel-Aviv. "J’ai vraiment peur de ce qui va se passer ici." Gadi Eisenkot, qui a perdu son fils de 25 ans et deux neveux dans le conflit dans la bande de Gaza, a accusé Benjamin Netanyahu de "s'appuyer sur une campagne fondée sur la politique de la peur, les mensonges et les menaces", et s'est dit convaincu que Donald Trump travaillerait "en totale coopération avec quelque dirigeant choisi par le peuple". "Je suis convaincu qu’à la fin de la journée, nous assisterons à un changement — un nouvel élan pour l’État d’Israël — qui servira de réparation pour ces trois dernières années et pour cette terrible journée", a déclaré l'ancien officier lors d’une visite au kibboutz Nir Oz dans le sud d’Israël, cible des attaques du 7-Octobre. Il a voté au côté de Gadi Mozes, l’un des 251 otages enlevés alors par le Hamas. À l’instar de Benjamin Netanyahu et de la quasi-totalité des partis juifs, Gadi Eisenkot s’oppose à la création d'un Etat palestinien. Il s'est toutefois montré critique envers les violences commises par les colons juifs à l’encontre des Palestiniens en Cisjordanie occupée, lesquelles sont en recrudescence depuis 2023. RÉSULTATS OFFICIELS DANS UNE SEMAINE Les électeurs issus de la minorité arabe d'Israël — israéliens de nationalité mais palestiniens d'origine — se mobilisent en un nombre "sans précédent", a affirmé le candidat palestinien Ahmed Tibi. Gadi Eisenkot a exclu tout partenariat avec les partis arabes, invoquant un manque de valeurs communes. Certains experts estiment toutefois que ceux-ci soutiendraient son gouvernement afin de garantir le départ de Benjamin Netanyahu. Ce dernier a qualifié à plusieurs reprises les électeurs arabo-israéliens de menace, utilisant des termes que ses adversaires jugent racistes. Des voitures arborant les drapeaux du Likoud ont sillonné les rues de Jérusalem mardi, équipées de haut-parleurs diffusant à plein volume l'appel islamique à la prière et proclamant: "Sortez de chez vous tout de suite. Les Arabes votent." Les électeurs sont appelés à renouveler les 120 membres de la Knesset - l'unique chambre du Parlement israélien - pour un mandat de quatre ans, selon un mode de scrutin proportionnel par liste. Pour être représentée au Parlement, une liste doit recueillir au moins 3,25% des voix, ce qui lui permet d'obtenir quatre sièges. Aucun parti n'a jamais réussi à emporter seul la majorité absolue (61 sièges) et les gouvernements sont donc le fruit de coalitions, parfois fragiles. Ce système accorde une grande importance aux petits partis, souvent indispensables à la formation d'une coalition viable. Les Premiers ministres sont ainsi régulièrement contraints de satisfaire leurs exigences pour garantir la survie de leur cabinet. Ainsi Benjamin Netanyahu, qui pourrait de nouveau tirer parti de cette fragmentation politique, mais reste tributaire de l'appui des figures de l'extrême droite [USN:L8N46613P TEXT:"Itamar Ben-Gvir"], qui a voté dans une colonie cisjordanienne de Kiryat Arba, et Bezalel Smotrich, cibles de sanctions de la part de certains pays occidentaux. Les résultats définitifs de l'élection sont attendus d'ici au 30 octobre et seront officiellement annoncés le 4 novembre. Le président Isaac Herzog engagera ensuite des consultations politiques en vue de la formation d'un gouvernement. Le futur Premier ministre dispose de 42 jours pour mener à bien la constitution de son équipe. Si ni Benjamin Netanyahu ni Gadi Eisenkot ne parviennent à former une coalition gouvernementale, l'actuel Premier ministre pourrait rester en fonction à titre intérimaire jusqu'à la tenue de nouvelles élections.

item.title: Gold gains on softer oil prices ahead of Fed meeting
item.description: Gold prices rose about 1% on Tuesday as lower oil prices lent support, with market participants awaiting the Federal Reserve's policy meeting for signals on the future path of US interest rates.
item.dc:creator: Vishak Mathew
item.content:encoded: Gold prices rose about 1% on Tuesday as lower oil prices lent support, with market participants awaiting the Federal Reserve's policy meeting for signals on the future path of US interest rates. Spot gold climbed 0.9% to $4,051.78 per ounce by 10:59 a.m. ET (1459 GMT) after hitting as low as $3,987.14 earlier in the session. US gold futures for December delivery rose 0.69% to $4,066.40 per ounce. "Softer oil prices will probably provide some lift for gold because it relieves the inflation worries and arguably moderates Fed hawkishness to some degree," said Peter Grant, vice president and senior metals strategist at Zaner Metals. "I think the market is just merely trading at this point off Middle East headlines and ongoing negotiations," Grant added. Oil futures fell more than 1% on Tuesday as attention turned to Middle East peace talks, though prices remain near multi-month highs as the Houthi-Saudi Arabia conflict rages and the potential for fresh US-Israeli attacks hangs over the market. However, "if crude oil prices are going to continue to rise, that's going to cause problematic price inflation, and that's going to cause central banks to tighten their monetary policy. And that's bearish for gold," said Jim Wyckoff, a market analyst at American Gold Exchange. [USN:L6N46518P TEXT:"Federal Reserve policymakers"] have telegraphed they will not raise US short-term borrowing costs again this week, but with inflation concerns still front and center, investors believe a rate-hike pause will not last for long. Higher rates increase the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding gold. Traders are now pricing in an 83% probability of a US rate hike in December, according to the CME's FedWatch Tool . Investors also await US Personal Consumption Expenditures data due on Thursday, the gauge the Fed watches most closely as it targets 2% inflation. Analysts cut their 2026 gold price forecast for a second straight quarter because of high Treasury yields, a strong US dollar and expectations that rates will stay high for longer, but still expect a recovery in 2027, a Reuters survey shows. Among other metals, spot silver rose 0.8% to $54.37 per ounce after hitting its lowest in almost a year, platinum edged up 0.3% to $1,531.95 after falling to its lowest since late November 2025 and palladium dropped 1.4% to $1,035.00 after slipping to its lowest since June 2025, earlier in the session.

item.title: Alibaba wins injunction against Pentagon contract restrictions tied to China blacklist
item.description: A US federal judge on Monday granted Alibaba Group Holding's request for a preliminary injunction, ordering the US government not to deny Pentagon contracts to companies because they, their parent companies or subsidiaries do business with firms that engage in lobbying activities for the e-commerce giant.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Baptista, Laurie Chen
item.content:encoded: A US federal judge on Monday granted Alibaba Group Holding's (9988.HK) request for a preliminary injunction, ordering the US government not to deny Pentagon contracts to companies because they, their parent companies or subsidiaries do business with firms that engage in lobbying activities for the e-commerce giant. Alibaba [USN:L1N42V0RB TEXT:"sued"] the US government in June after the Pentagon added it to a [USN:FWN42G12Z TEXT:"list of companies"] allegedly aiding China's military, alongside internet search provider Baidu, EV maker BYD and other major Chinese manufacturing and technology firms. Monday's ruling means Alibaba will be able to retain US lobbyists who also represent Pentagon contractors, removing a potential obstacle to the company's efforts to challenge its designation as a Chinese military company. Alibaba fired dozens of its Washington lobbyists after the Pentagon action in June, according to a source with direct knowledge of the matter who was not authorised to speak to the media. The designation does not impose formal sanctions, but restricts Pentagon contracts with listed companies and, from 2027, purchases of their products or services through third parties. Other listed Chinese tech firms were also concerned about the designation's impact on international lobbying activities as well as the indirect procurement ban, which would completely remove Chinese products from US defence contractors' supply chains, the source added. Alibaba has denied any military ties, saying its products and services are built for retail, logistics, and enterprise technology rather than defence or intelligence. "The determinations have no basis in fact or law," Alibaba said in its lawsuit in June, seeking its removal from the list. Monday's injunction does not remove Alibaba from the Pentagon list, which the company is continuing to challenge in court. Alibaba did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the injunction. COMPANIES TAKE LEGAL ACTION Alibaba is one of several Chinese firms taking legal action to challenge their placement on the Pentagon's list. Last month, two subsidiaries of the world's largest electric vehicle maker BYD (002594.SZ) sued the US Department of Defence over a federal law banning any Pentagon contractors from hiring lobbyists that also work with blacklisted firms, arguing that it breached BYD's First Amendment rights. In August, DJI, the world's largest drone maker, [USN:L6N44B0VR TEXT:"appealed"] its inclusion on the blacklist with the court finding merit in its argument that unclassified records did not support the conclusion that the company contributed to the Chinese defence industrial base. The appeals court ordered the lower court to reconsider its decision to reject DJI's bid to be removed from the Pentagon list and the case is ongoing. The same month, biotech firm WuXi AppTec Co (603259.SS) also won a preliminary [USN:L1N4440V2 TEXT:"injunction"] from a US federal court, which blocked its inclusion on the list. WuXi said the Pentagon designation was politically motivated.

item.title: Singapore, Indonesia eye haze task force, reaffirm ties amid tensions, ministers say
item.description: Indonesia and Singapore are looking to set up a joint task force to deal with haze from Indonesia's wildfires, the countries' foreign ministers said on Tuesday, as they met to reaffirm their ties after weeks of simmering tensions.
item.dc:creator: Stanley Widianto, Xinghui Kok
item.content:encoded: Indonesia and Singapore are looking to set up a joint task force to deal with haze from Indonesia's wildfires, the countries' foreign ministers said on Tuesday, as they met to reaffirm their ties after weeks of simmering tensions. The visit to Jakarta by Singapore Foreign Minister Vivian Balakrishnan came amid mounting frustrations in the city-state over the transboundary haze generated by Indonesia's [USN:L6N4610CY TEXT:"most intense"] forest fires in 11 years. After a two-hour meeting, Singapore and Indonesia's top diplomats discussed establishing a task force that would enable the countries to share information, gather cross-border evidence and potentially even recover assets from companies linked to the forest fires, Indonesia's Foreign Minister Arrmanatha Nasir said. "We must follow the money trail these companies have left behind. Singapore offered to share data on companies linked to the fires," Nasir said. "No border should shield those who profit from burning our forests." Indonesia has previously launched criminal investigations into companies linked to the fires. Nasir added that the two countries were mature enough to talk candidly about the fires, which have caused a spike in respiratory illnesses in Indonesia and engulfed neighbouring Singapore, Malaysia and East Timor in smoke. "Singapore stands in solidarity with Indonesia. (Haze) is a common problem, and one that we can best achieve collectively," Balakrishnan said after the meeting. Both foreign ministers said on Tuesday that the first victims of the haze were Indonesians, with Balakrishnan vowing to crack down on companies registered in Singapore found to be responsible for the fires. GAS SUPPLY CUTS In their remarks, neither minister mentioned the tensions arising from Jakarta's decision to cut [USN:L6N46A01Z TEXT:"gas supplies"] to the city-state. Jakarta cut pipelined gas to Singapore by about 8% as of Saturday, saying it was safeguarding domestic supplies. [USN:L4N45T0LE TEXT:"Singapore generates"] up to 95% of its electricity from natural gas, and though the supply cut from Indonesia amounts to less than 2% of daily demand, Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said on Sunday that he expects contract signatories to "honour their commitments". Indonesia's energy minister, Bahlil Lahadalia, [USN:L6N46C0FK TEXT:"hit back"] on Monday, saying the amount of gas now being supplied to Singapore met the minimum level stipulated under their agreement. "Our nation is a nation that honours contracts, rules. So don't lecture Indonesia on how to honour contracts," Bahlil said. Veteran Singaporean diplomat Bilahari Kausikan called the gas cuts an "attempt at intimidation" but said they would be ineffectual. Singapore's state investor Temasek and its sovereign wealth fund GIC were also on the defensive last week, rejecting allegations by a former Indonesian trade minister that they had pressured global index provider MSCI to consider demoting Indonesia's equities to [USN:L6N46208E TEXT:""standalone" market status"]. Indonesia's government has not commented on the allegation by the former minister.

item.title: Dollar edges higher as focus turns to central bank meetings
item.description: The dollar firmed against major currencies including the euro, yen and sterling on Tuesday amid market positioning ahead of a series of central bank meetings for fresh clues on the economic outlook and the path of interest rates.
item.dc:creator: Alun John, Chibuike Oguh
item.content:encoded: The dollar firmed against major currencies including the euro, yen and sterling on Tuesday amid market positioning ahead of a series of central bank meetings for fresh clues on the economic outlook and the path of interest rates. The Federal Reserve is set to announce its latest policy decision on Wednesday, the European Central Bank is up on Thursday, and the Bank of Japan rounds out the week on Friday. All three are expected to keep rates on hold, so the focus will be on any hints that policymakers give on their outlooks. The dollar has also stabilized after it came under pressure following a selloff in high-flying AI stocks last week. The euro was down 0.25% against the dollar at $1.1144. "The dollar has rebounded ahead of the Fed meeting and AI sentiment has stabilized a little bit after last week," said Kevin Ford, FX and macro strategist at Convera. "The dollar was caught in the crossfire last week as an extension of the equity distress, high oil prices and what's happening with European fiscal stress coming from France. So I think what markets have done is to take a little bit of the pressure off the Fed to hike rates." The euro was on track to be the worst-performing developed-market currency in October, down 1.65% on the dollar, bruised by high energy costs, the volatility in French government bonds and worries about France's fiscal position. The single currency extended its fall slightly after the release of the [USN:L5N46D0P6 TEXT:"ECB's quarterly Bank Lending Survey"], which showed the impact of its rate hikes becoming visible. If that trend continues, it could, at the margin, reduce pressure on the ECB to continue with rate hikes deep into next year. Meanwhile, Japanese Finance Minister [USN:L2N46D03K TEXT:"Satsuki Katayama"] said the government stood ready to take decisive action in the currency market, reminding markets of its willingness to prop up its currency. The yen was among the best-performing major currencies last week, strengthening around 0.75% on the dollar, its biggest weekly gain since early September, as AI jitters in the equity market spurred a rush into the currency. The dollar was up 0.15% to 157.73 against the Japanese yen . Sterling weakened 0.16% against the dollar to $1.3317. The dollar index , which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies including the yen and the euro, rose 0.2% to 102.22. The [USN:L6N4690QQ TEXT:"Reserve Bank of New Zealand"] and the Bank of Canada also announce their policy decisions on Wednesday, with both expected to raise interest rates. The New Zealand dollar strengthened 0.33% versus the greenback to $0.5699. The Canadian dollar weakened 0.14% versus the greenback to C$1.404 per dollar.

item.title: Israelis shatter turnout records to pass wartime judgment on Netanyahu
item.description: Israelis surged to the polls on Tuesday at a pace that shattered records, to pass wartime judgment on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in what voters described as the most consequential election in the nation's history.
item.dc:creator: Steven Scheer, Alexander Cornwell
item.content:encoded: Israelis surged to the polls on Tuesday at a pace that shattered records, to pass wartime judgment on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in what voters described as the most consequential election in the nation's history. Long lines formed outside polling stations for the first election since the October 7, 2023, Hamas-led attacks, with voters passionately engaged over the trauma of the country's deadliest day and the ensuing wars in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran. The Central Elections Committee reported that 44.9% of eligible voters had already cast their ballots within the first seven hours of voting, with eight more hours to go. That "broke all records", it said. Policies of Netanyahu's right-wing coalition have been divisive at home and have deepened Israel's international isolation, while he has defended his record, calling himself the only leader with the mettle to face down Israel's foes. Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving leader with 19 years in office, is an unmatched political survivor, and his nationalist politics are increasingly entrenched. Israel's fragmented system makes it difficult for an array of opponents to force out his coalition of right-wing, far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties. His main rival [USN:L6N46303T TEXT:"Gadi Eisenkot"], a military ex-chief of staff and security hawk, aims to unseat him with the support of parties on the right and centre, as well as the rump of an increasingly marginalised left. Opinion polls show a close race , with neither leader facing an easy path to power. Forecasters were hesitant to guess what impact the unprecedented turnout might have on the result. A surge in votes from Israelis of Palestinian heritage could limit gains for Netanyahu's right-wing coalition, while increasing the odds that any government formed to oust him would require Arab parties' support, a contentious prospect among Jewish party leaders. In a message to supporters more than five hours after polls opened, Netanyahu urged them to vote, saying turnout was high among his opponents on the left and among Israelis of Arab heritage, around a fifth of the country. "We need it to be high too. You all need to stream to the polls," he said. "This is a fateful moment." VOTER SEES ELECTION AS MOST IMPORTANT SHE'S KNOWN "I think these elections are the most important of all the ones I’ve known," said Ruth Epstein, an 81-year-old longtime left-wing voter in Ramat Gan near Tel Aviv, who voted for the opposition Democrats. "I’m really scared about what will be here." Netanyahu has campaigned on an endorsement from US President Donald Trump , his ally in war against Iran , who has said they should "finish the job". If neither Netanyahu nor Eisenkot can form a governing coalition in the 120-seat parliament, Netanyahu could stay on as caretaker until another election is held. His opponents have managed to wrest him from the premiership only once since 2009, and that took four inconclusive elections in two years. He was back 18 months later. EISENKOT SEES 'NEW SPIRIT' For many of Netanyahu's opponents, the election turns on [USN:L8N4680E4 TEXT:"accountability"] for the security failures of October 7, Israel's deadliest day. Opposition groups have promised to hold a national inquiry, which Netanyahu's government has resisted. "I am convinced that by the end of today, we will see a change — a new spirit for the State of Israel — that will serve as a rectification for the past three years and for that terrible day," Eisenkot said during a visit to kibbutz Nir Oz in southern Israel, targeted in the October 7 attacks. He walked to the polls with Gadi Mozes, one of 251 people kidnapped by Hamas and taken to Gaza during the attack that killed 1,200 people. Eisenkot says Israel's response — a war which health authorities say killed more than 74,000 Palestinians — was a failure because Hamas remains in charge. He repeated his commitment to dismantle or destroy Hamas' military and governing power in Gaza within 18 months of forming a government. Itamar Ben-Gvir, leader of a far-right party in Netanyahu's coalition, cast his vote in the Kiryat Arba settlement in the occupied West Bank early on Tuesday. He predicted Netanyahu would return as prime minister and his own party would serve as the right-wing anchor of the government. ARAB TURNOUT COULD BE KEY Ahmed Tibi, a candidate from an Arab party, said the record turnout from [USN:L8N45Z09Z TEXT:"Israel's Arab minority"] would "pave the way for an alternative government and change the grave reality". Eisenkot has ruled out partnering with Arab parties, citing a lack of shared values, although some possible scenarios envision them propping up a minority government to topple Netanyahu. Netanyahu has repeatedly described Arab-Israeli voters as a threat in language his opponents say crosses into racism. He posted an AI-generated image on X on Tuesday showing Arabs including women in niqabs queuing at a polling station, and told his supporters they were in a battle for the country's future. Cars with flags of Netanyahu's Likud Party drove through the Jerusalem streets with loudspeakers blaring the Islamic call to prayer and saying: "Get out of your houses now. Arabs are voting." Like nearly all Jewish party leaders in Israel, Eisenkot opposes the two-state solution that once underpinned decades of peace negotiations with the Palestinians. But he has criticised Jewish settler violence against Palestinians in the Israeli-occupied West Bank, which has surged since 2023 and strained Israel's ties with Western states. And he opposes Netanyahu's far-right coalition partners. Israel flattened much of Gaza in the offensive launched after October 7, and now occupies around two-thirds of the enclave under a year-old US-brokered ceasefire. Negotiations for Hamas to disarm and Israel to withdraw have stalled. Israel also dealt heavy blows to Iran-backed Hezbollah in Lebanon, where it now occupies a swathe of territory, and traded strikes with Iran, leading to a 12-day air campaign in 2025 and this year's joint US-Israeli war.

item.title: UN inquiry says Israel kept committing genocide in Gaza after truce
item.description: Israel continued to commit genocide in Gaza after last October's US-brokered ceasefire in the enclave, a UN commission said in a report published on Monday that Israel dismissed as part of a "misinformation campaign".
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Israel continued to commit genocide in Gaza after last October's US-brokered ceasefire in the enclave, a UN commission said in a report published on Monday that Israel dismissed as part of a "misinformation campaign". The report by the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem, and Israel, examined violations against Palestinian civilians, including children, since the start of the war between Israel and Hamas on October 7, 2023, up to September this year. It said Israeli authorities had kept committing "genocidal acts with the genocidal intent to destroy, in whole or in part, the Palestinians in Gaza", and that the situation had also continued to deteriorate in the occupied West Bank. Another report by the commission in September last year found that Israel had [USN:L2N3V306V TEXT:"committed genocide in Gaza"] and that top Israeli officials including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu incited these acts — accusations that Israel called scandalous. The Israeli mission in Geneva said the latest report was part of a misinformation campaign to demonize the State of Israel. "The attempt to destroy the Jewish state ... continues today through efforts by actors such as the UN Commission of Inquiry to undermine Israel’s legitimacy and deny its fundamental right to exist and defend itself," Ambassador Daniel Meron said in a statement. HEAVY MUNITIONS HIT POPULATED AREAS, COMMISSION SAYS The commission found that Israeli forces continued using heavy munitions, drones, quadcopters, artillery and sniper fire in densely populated areas during the ceasefire in Gaza. It said the [USN:L1N3YO0RL TEXT:""Yellow Line", "]which was presented as a temporary ceasefire demarcation, was encroaching increasingly into Gaza, and becoming a de facto border, which the report said reflected Israel’s expanding territorial control of Gaza. Palestinian authorities say more than 74,000 people have been killed in Israel's assault on Gaza, launched after Hamas-led fighters killed about 1,200 people in southern Israel on October 7, 2023. In its report to the UN General Assembly, the commission said the situation in the West Bank had also deteriorated sharply, with the number of Palestinians killed in airstrikes increasing from six between 2008 and October 6, 2023, to 254 between October 7, 2023 and September 30, 2026. The report said Israeli military operations, alongside sustained settler violence, formed part of a widespread and systematic attack against the civilian population in the West Bank since October 7, 2023. "The Commission concludes that the Israeli authorities and forces have committed the crimes against humanity of extermination, torture, rape and other forms of sexual violence in the West Bank, as well as persecution based on intersecting discriminatory grounds, with nationality, race and ethnicity at its core." Commenting on the report, the Israeli mission said the international community should reject what it described as distortions, and "repudiate the Commission's findings". Commission Chair Srinivasan Muralidhar said the intentional killing of Palestinian civilians and destruction of homes in the West Bank formed part of a broader strategy to exterminate and displace Palestinians. Military operations since January 2025 have led to the largest displacement of Palestinians in the West Bank since 1967, with 34,176 Palestinians remaining displaced as of August 2026, the report said. The commission also faulted the Palestinian Authority, saying it had targeted Palestinians who voice dissenting views and that journalists and human rights defenders had been killed and injured.

item.title: Meta eyes record $97.5 billion equity raise to fund AI expansion
item.description: Meta Platforms on Tuesday raised the planned size of its largest-ever equity offerings to $97.5 billion, as the social media giant taps the public market to aggressively expand its AI infrastructure.
item.dc:creator: Jaspreet Singh
item.content:encoded: Meta Platforms (META.O) on Tuesday raised the planned size of its largest-ever equity offerings to $97.5 billion, as the social media giant taps the public market to aggressively expand its AI infrastructure. The fundraising plan, among the biggest by an AI company, has also drawn interest of up to $5 billion in total from Nvidia (NVDA.O) , Advanced Micro Devices (AMD.O) and Broadcom (AVGO.O) for Class A common shares. Their funding interest adds to concerns about an increasingly circular flow of capital in the AI industry, as chip suppliers help finance the expansion of one of their biggest customers. Meta has been pouring money into chips and data centers to compete better with OpenAI and Anthropic. Meta now plans to raise $25 billion in common stock at $625 per share, compared with $22.5 billion disclosed on Monday. It also priced 250 million convertible preferred depositary shares at $50 apiece, for a total offering value of $12.5 billion. The Facebook parent's shares closed down nearly 2% at $630.56 on Monday. The stock was down about 1% on Tuesday. The social media company also has a separate program to sell up to $60 billion in shares over time at prevailing market prices. While Meta has not yet finalized the timing and terms for its at-the-market offering, it expects the sale to begin after its planned non-voting Class C shares start trading in the first quarter of 2027. "We expect investors to continue to question the financing and potential for future capital raises," William Blair analysts said on Monday. "Overall, we believe the financing reinforces both Meta's confidence in the long-term returns from AI investment and the increasingly capital-intensive nature of pursuing that opportunity." On Tuesday, Nvidia and AMD separately announced investments of [USN:L6N46D0BE TEXT:"$3 billion"] and $1 billion, respectively, in Meta's equity offering. Meta's latest fundraising further underscores a shift among companies increasingly tapping debt markets and raising equity to bolster their AI infrastructure, after previously relying on cash to fund their investments. Alphabet (GOOGL.O) had [USN:L4N42B1AK TEXT:"increased"] its equity offerings to $84.75 billion in June. SpaceX on Monday said an affiliate of Apollo Global Management (APO.N) will buy AI chips and server hardware and lease them to the rockets-to-AI firm, in a deal with total principal payments of [USN:L6N46C0RJ TEXT:"about $40 billion"]. META'S AI SPENDING IS BURNING CASH Meta has committed to spending about $825 billion in the future, driven primarily by growing investments in data centers, AI-related infrastructure, and cloud computing power. But the aggressive expansion has eroded its historically strong free cash flow. The company reported a $2.12 billion cash burn in the third quarter, its first negative free cash flow in over a decade, compared with a positive cash flow of $10.63 billion a year ago. Still, the early popularity of [USN:L6N4500XV TEXT:"its consumer-focused AI agent Muse"] and release of a competitive new [USN:L4N45Y13Q TEXT:"series of AI models"] have helped partly justify Meta's aggressive investments. "We believe that Meta will ultimately produce a profitable AI business and its returns longer-term should help the company diversify, although the path may not be linear," William Blair analysts said. The company had $82.45 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities and $80.92 billion in long-term debt as of September 30, according to its latest quarterly filing. Last week, Meta raised the lower end of its annual [USN:L4N4671S3 TEXT:"capital expenditure"] forecast to $135 billion to $145 billion. The company said it would issue Class C common stock in January 2027, effectively creating a two-for-one split, to fund acquisitions and retain top talent while maintaining CEO Mark Zuckerberg's control. Meta [USN:L6N46801B TEXT:"agreed to grant Zuckerberg Class C shares"] he can sell to help pay a potential California billionaire wealth tax, in exchange for his commitment to remain in California.

item.title: UBS says does not permit use of external AI models for client transactions
item.description: Swiss bank UBS will not allow the use of external AI models to execute actions on behalf of clients, CEO Sergio Ermotti said on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Swiss bank UBS (UBSG.S) will not allow the use of external AI models to execute actions on behalf of clients, CEO Sergio Ermotti said on Tuesday. Concerns that sophisticated AI agents could harm the financial system have risen within the banking industry. Major US banks have been [USN:L6N4680PX TEXT:"blocking"] third-party AI agents' access to customer accounts, people familiar with the matter have said. "You heard recently some banks are being exposed to potential misbehaviors of models in managing clients' accounts and shifting deposits and optimizing deposits," Ermotti told an event at Zurich's ETH university, the SCION Day 2026 conference. "We are not allowing models to enter into the bank and do that." "When you talk about AI, the most important issue right now is to make sure that we don't get AI models that drive outcomes for clients in a black box," he added. UBS' integration of fallen rival Credit Suisse, which it acquired after the bank collapsed in 2023, forced it to slow its deployment of AI somewhat, but now the lender can put even more emphasis on technology, Ermotti said. "I'm glad that we are almost over with the integration and therefore we can now put even more emphasis around technology and how we can help the bank become more effective and efficient," he said. UBS has said it expects to largely conclude the integration of Credit Suisse by the end of this year.

item.description: Wall Street ouvre en hausse à la veille de la décision de la Fed
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Wall Street ouvre en hausse à la veille de la décision de la Fed 27 octobre (Reuters) - La Bourse de New York a ouvert en hausse mardi, rassurée par les premières publications de résultats d'entreprises à la veille des annonces de politique monétaire de la Réserve fédérale. Etats-Unis: La confiance des consommateurs progresse plus que prévu en octobre 27 octobre (Reuters) - La confiance des consommateurs aux États-Unis s'est améliorée plus que prévu en octobre, selon l'enquête mensuelle du Conference Board publiée mardi. Zone euro: La croissance des prêts aux entreprises se maintient en septembre, selon la BCE 27 octobre (Reuters) - La croissance des prêts aux entreprises dans la zone euro est restée stable en septembre, montrent les données publiées mardi par la Banque centrale européenne (BCE). Zone euro: Net recul de la demande de prêts immobiliers sur fond de hausse des taux, selon une enquête BCE FRANCFORT, 27 octobre (Reuters) - La demande de prêts immobiliers dans la zone euro a considérablement reculé au cours du troisième trimestre, dans un contexte de hausse des taux d'intérêt et de resserrement des conditions de crédit, montre une enquête publiée mardi par la Banque centrale européenne (BCE). France-La confiance des ménages à son plus bas depuis 2013 en octobre 27 octobre (Reuters) - La confiance des ménages en France a baissé plus que prévu au mois d'octobre, atteignant son niveau le plus bas depuis juin 2013, montre l'enquête mensuelle de conjoncture publiée mardi par l'Insee. Boeing: Les difficultés dans la production d'avions de ligne pèsent sur les résultats du 3e trimestre SEATTLE, 27 octobre (Reuters) - Boeing a annoncé mardi une perte plus importante que prévu au troisième trimestre, les difficultés liées à la chaîne d’approvisionnement et les retards de production au sein de sa division d’avions commerciaux ayant éclipsé l’amélioration des marges enregistrée dans le reste de l’entreprise. Coca-Cola relève son objectif annuel de bénéfice grâce à la demande en boissons et sodas 27 octobre (Reuters) - Coca-Cola a réhaussé mardi son objectif de bénéfice annuel, le groupe misant sur la résilience de la demande pour ses sodas sans sucre et ses boissons à prix plus élevés, telles que le lait "Fairlife" et les boissons gazeuses. Le rendement de l'OAT repart à la hausse après une accalmie de courte durée 27 octobre (Reuters) - Les taux d'emprunt de la France repartent à la hausse mardi après un recul net mais de courte durée la veille, ce qui met en évidence les défis auxquels la deuxième économie de la zone euro continue de faire face dans un contexte d'incertitude budgétaire et politique. Orange relève ses perspectives 2026 avec la croissance hors de France 27 octobre (Reuters) - Orange a relevé mardi son objectif de marge opérationnelle annuel, l'opérateur français de télécommunications citant notamment ses performances dans la région Afrique et Moyen-Orient, où il affiche une croissance à deux chiffres, ainsi qu'en Pologne et en Espagne. UPS rehausse ses prévisions avec les envois à forte valeur ajoutée 27 octobre (Reuters) - United Parcel Service a revu à la hausse mardi ses prévisions de chiffre d'affaires et de bénéfice annuels, misant sur les expéditions aériennes internationales à forte marge après avoir décidé de supprimer des millions de livraisons à faible marge pour son plus gros client, Amazon.com.

item.description: La Jordanie dit avoir tué plus de 20 combattants de l'EI en Syrie
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La Jordanie dit avoir tué plus de 20 combattants de l'EI en Syrie 27 octobre (Reuters) - La Jordanie a tué plus de 20 combattants du groupe État islamique (EI) lors de frappes aériennes menées lundi soir dans le sud de la Syrie, à la suite d'un attentat meurtrier perpétré contre une église en Jordanie, a déclaré mardi le ministre de la Communication, Mohamed al Momani. Brésil: Le parti de Bolsonaro reconnaît le résultat de la présidentielle SÃO PAULO, 26 octobre (Reuters) - Le parti de Flavio Bolsonaro a reconnu lundi le résultat de l'élection présidentielle au Brésil, qui a vu le président sortant Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva obtenir un quatrième mandat, dans un communiqué. "Retour vers le futur" au Brésil? Flavio Bolsonaro, comme jadis son père, refuse de reconnaître la victoire de Lula SÃO PAULO, 26 octobre (Reuters) - Le candidat de la droite brésilienne Flavio Bolsonaro emboîte le pas à son père, l'ex-président condamné pour tentative de coup d'Etat après la présidentielle perdue de 2022, en refusant de reconnaître sa défaite face au président sortant Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, qui a remporté dimanche un quatrième mandat historique. La Jordanie dit avoir frappé des repaires de combattants en Syrie après l'attaque contre une église AL-JUDAYYDA, Jordanie, LE CAIRE, 26 octobre (Reuters) - La Jordanie a déclaré lundi que ses forces aériennes ont frappé des repaires de combattants dans le sud de la Syrie en réponse à l'attaque meurtrière de vendredi contre une église dans le sud du pays. Ukraine-Cessez-le-feu à Olechky, les bombardements continuent ailleurs 27 octobre (Reuters) - La Russie et l'Ukraine ont annoncé mardi qu'un cessez-le-feu localisé avait débuté afin de permettre une opération humanitaire dans la ville d'Olechky, contrôlée par Moscou dans le sud de l'Ukraine, tout en poursuivant leurs frappes respectives sur les autres fronts, notamment à Kyiv. Israël: Forte participation aux législatives, Netanyahu appelle ses partisans à se mobiliser JÉRUSALEM, 27 octobre (Reuters) - Les quelque 7,3 millions d'électeurs israéliens se pressaient mardi aux urnes pour décider du sort du Premier ministre sortant Benjamin Netanyahu lors des élections législatives, premier scrutin national depuis le choc des attaques meurtrières du Hamas le 7 octobre 2023. Washington et Ottawa négocient pour alléger les droits de douane sur l'acier et les véhicules canadiens, selon des sources OTTAWA/WASHINGTON, 26 octobre (Reuters) - - Les Etats-Unis et le Canada négocient pour atténuer les droits de douane américains sur l'acier et les véhicules canadiens, a-t-on appris lundi de deux sources américaines et quatre sources canadiennes, alors que les deux gouvernements cherchent à renouer des liens distendus après l'échec des négociations commerciales cet été. Le pape se rendra comme prévu en Amérique latine en novembre CITE DU VATICAN, 26 octobre (Reuters) - Le pape Léon XIV, opéré le 13 octobre dernier d'une tumeur cancéreuse au poumon droit, se rendra comme prévu en Uruguay, en Argentine et au Pérou du 6 au 17 novembre prochains, ses médecins estimant qu'il est suffisamment remis pour effectuer ce voyage, annonce lundi le Vatican. Russie: Arrestation de deux suspects après une tentative d'attaque pour le compte de l'Ukraine annonce le FSB Le renseignement russe (FSB) a annoncé lundi l'arrestation de deux hommes soupçonnés d'une tentative d'attaque de drones pour le compte de l'Ukraine contre la défense anti-aérienne russe à Moscou et une installation électrique de la capitale. Jordanie: Arrestation de trois suspects après une attaque meurtrière contre une église Les forces de sécurité jordaniennes ont arrêté trois suspects après l'attaque meurtrière perpétrée vendredi contre une église dans le sud du pays, rapporte lundi la télévision d'État.
